Lebih dari itu, apakah ada tautan ke studi yang mendukung apa yang diklaim? Jika ada, seberapa besar studi itu? Jika sebuah studi hanya melibatkan 12 orang, itu tidak cukup besar untuk memberikan informasi yang akurat.

    Robert Harris membuat akronim CARS, yang membantu memilah apakah informasi di suatu situs web valid. Kredibilitas, Akurasi masa lalu, Rasionalitas, dan Informasi pendukung semuanya penting untuk dilihat agar kita tahu apakah kita harus menghargai informasi di situs tersebut.2

    Sayangnya, banyak orang yang mengklaim memiliki jawaban untuk hidup panjang dan sehat sebenarnya sedang mencoba menjual buku, suplemen, dan berbagai produk lainnya. Seorang dokter terkenal yang mempromosikan kesehatan lebih baik melalui penggunaan suplemen (yang ia jual) berhasil mengumpulkan cukup banyak uang sehingga ia menyatakan dalam sebuah pernyataan tertulis tahun 2017 bahwa kekayaannya melebihi 100 juta dolar. Ini tidak berarti ia tidak ada yang bisa ditawarkan, tetapi hal ini menunjukkan bahwa ia memiliki bias terhadap merekomendasikan barang yang ia jual.

    Asosiasi Medis Amerika memiliki pedoman agar dokter dapat menjual produk dari praktik mereka secara etis. Pedoman itu menyatakan bahwa produk harus memenuhi kebutuhan mendesak tertentu (misalnya, kruk di praktik Ortopedi), memiliki validitas ilmiah untuk penggunaannya, dan dokter harus menawarkan informasi tentang cara lain agar pasien dapat memperoleh produk yang sama di tempat lain.3 Lebih dari itu, dokter harus mengungkapkan kepada pasiennya setiap kepentingan finansial yang mereka miliki terhadap produk yang ditawarkan kepada pasien.

    Bias Konfirmasi

    Kebanyakan dari kita membaca untuk mengonfirmasi hal-hal yang sudah kita percayai. Saya melihat ini ketika orang membaca Alkitab— entah bagaimana, orang dapat membaca Alkitab dan sepenuhnya mengabaikan ayat-ayat yang bertentangan dengan perilaku mereka dalam hal keterlibatan politik atau kesopanan berpakaian tetapi percaya bahwa mereka mengikuti seluruh firman Kitab Suci.

    Dengan cara yang sama, masing-masing dari kita dapat menemukan cerita dan informasi yang memperkuat keyakinan kita tentang dokter dan kedokteran. Jika kita percaya bahwa dokter hanya mengejar uang dan tidak etis serta meresepkan obat yang beracun bagi pasien, kita dapat menemukan artikel yang mengonfirmasi itu. Sebaliknya, jika kita mencari cerita yang merobohkan teori pengobatan alternatif, kita juga dapat menemukan artikel-artikel itu.

    Yang penting adalah kita mendekati pertanyaan dengan mencari jawaban nyata dan memahami bahwa ilmu pengetahuan tidak mengetahui segalanya.

    Sebagai contoh, kita tidak memiliki perawatan yang baik untuk orang yang mengalami gejala Long COVID. Itu tidak berarti bahwa banyak orang yang menderita COVID beberapa bulan kemudian tidak menderita dari hal-hal seperti kabut mental dan kelelahan, tetapi itu berarti bahwa tidak ada satu obat pun yang dalam studi terbukti lebih baik daripada pil gula untuk menghilangkan gejala-gejala tersebut.

    Dalam ketiadaan rencana perawatan yang terbukti secara ilmiah, banyak klinik mengembangkan jalur perawatan mereka sendiri, menggunakan campuran suplemen dan bahkan terapi oksigen hiperbarik. Apakah ini membantu? Saya tidak tahu, tetapi saya tahu bahwa mereka yang memasarkannya akan dengan percaya diri mengklaim bahwa mereka memiliki tingkat keberhasilan yang sangat tinggi dalam menyembuhkan orang jika mereka bersedia mengikuti (dan membayar) rencana perawatan tersebut.

    Lebih dari itu, ketika orang meneliti gejalanya, mereka cenderung memilih diagnosis yang mereka anggap mungkin berdasarkan tipe kepribadian mereka yang mendasarinya. Beberapa orang cenderung bermegah-catastrofi— yaitu, mereka segera mempercayai hasil terburuk dari skenario apa pun yang mereka hadapi. Orang-orang ini akan mengetik gejalanya dan sampai pada kesimpulan bahwa mereka mengidap kanker dengan hanya beberapa hari atau minggu untuk hidup. Seperti yang diberitahukan Allah kepada Hizkia, sudah waktunya bagi mereka untuk menata rumah mereka.

    Di sisi lain, banyak orang yang berkepribadian optimis. Mereka mengetik daftar gejala mereka dan sampai pada kesimpulan bahwa mereka menderita penyakit virus ringan dan akan merasa lebih baik dalam beberapa hari.

    Seluruh tujuan memiliki penyedia medis meninjau hal-hal adalah supaya praktisi dapat (semoga) memilah yang mungkin dari yang tidak mungkin. Mereka tidak berurusan dengan lapisan emosional yang dimiliki pasien, sehingga mereka dapat secara objektif memutuskan berapa banyak tes yang harus dipesan dan jenis tes apa yang harus dipesan untuk menghasilkan diagnosis.

    Dokter Dapat Mengidentifikasi Situasi Berbahaya

    Saya ingat melihat seorang pasien beberapa tahun lalu yang datang kepada saya dengan apa yang menurutnya infeksi sinus. Dia berusia sekitar 20-an dan mengatakan bahwa ia merasakan denyutan hebat di kepalanya dan banyak tekanan.

    Ia sebenarnya tidak memiliki lendir atau demam dan tidak ada gejala khas infeksi sinus, tetapi sinusitis tampak seperti diagnosis paling mungkin yang bisa ia pikirkan.

    Saya sekali lihat padanya dan tidak suka apa yang saya lihat. Salah satunya, dia sangat pucat. Selain itu, denyut jantungnya cukup cepat—130 denyut per menit saat istirahat. Ketika saya memeriksanya, saya tidak menemukan apa pun yang menunjukkan bahwa ia memiliki infeksi sinus.

    “Jenny,” saya katakan padanya. “Saya perlu kamu pergi ke rumah sakit dan mendapatkan hitung darah segera. Saya khawatir kamu benar-benar menderita anemia—meskipun saya tidak tahu mengapa. Tunggu di laboratorium dan saya akan bicara denganmu setelah saya mendapatkan hasilnya.”

    Kurang lebih 20 menit kemudian saya mendapat panggilan mendesak dari laboratorium rumah sakit. “Dr. Waldron,” suara di ujung sana berkata. “Kami memiliki hasil laboratorium kritis untuk Anda…”

    Hemoglobin Jenny adalah 4,6 (normal antara 12 dan 16), dan dia akhirnya mendapatkan transfusi. Yang tidak ia dapatkan adalah perawatan untuk infeksi sinus.

    Sakit dada adalah gejala klasik yang dapat menunjuk pada kondisi jantung yang mendasari. Pada saat yang sama, itu juga bisa sekadar menunjukkan refluks esofagus (asam di esofagus) atau peradangan pada tulang rusuk atau otot. Saya mungkin menemui beberapa pasien setiap hari yang memiliki gejala ini.

    Kebanyakan dari mereka membutuhkan pengobatan sederhana, tetapi beberapa dari mereka perlu segera dikirim ke rumah sakit untuk evaluasi jantung lengkap. Saya tidak tahu bagaimana mesin pencari online akan tahu arah mana yang harus ditunjukkan kepada seseorang setelah menelaah gejalanya.

    Paling tidak, sumber daya daring akan merujuk pengguna untuk mencari layanan darurat atau dokter setempat mereka.

    Tidak Semua Dokter Sama

    Sekitar 50 persen dokter lulus di paruh bawah kelas Sekolah Kedokteran mereka. Hanya karena seseorang tidak memiliki nilai tertinggi di Sekolah Kedokteran tidak berarti mereka tidak memiliki pengetahuan yang memadai untuk mengobati suatu penyakit. Mungkin pengetahuan paling penting yang dibutuhkan dokter adalah mengetahui kapan ia tidak tahu.

    Masih sulit bagi pasien untuk mengetahui apakah mereka berurusan dengan seseorang yang akan membantu mereka. Ketika Anda bertemu dokter, Anda cenderung menilai mereka berdasarkan “sikap di samping tempat tidur” mereka. Kebanyakan dari kita mencari seseorang yang memancarkan kepercayaan diri dan tampak tahu apa yang mereka lakukan.

    Kepercayaan diri tidak sama dengan kompetensi, dan ada banyak dokter (serta orang di bidang lain) yang memiliki tingkat kepercayaan diri tinggi tetapi tidak benar-benar kompeten untuk menangani situasi yang ada.

    Di sinilah melakukan sedikit penelitian dapat membantu. Pertama, dokter Anda memiliki ulasan daring, dan ulasan-ulasan itu akan menunjukkan sesuatu tentang tingkat perawatan yang mereka berikan kepada pasien. Kedua, jika apa yang diberitahukan penyedia layanan kesehatan Anda tampak aneh, mudah untuk melakukan sedikit penelitian tentang kondisi yang konon Anda hadapi dan melihat apakah gejalanya sesuai dan apakah pengobatannya tampak masuk akal.

    Penting untuk menyadari bahwa manusia tidak seperti kendaraan. Maksud saya adalah tidak ada alat pemindai yang dapat dipasang oleh penyedia layanan kesehatan yang menghasilkan semua kode kesalahan dan kemudian memperbaiki hal-hal yang menghasilkan kode-kode tersebut.

    Bahkan jika penyedia layanan kesehatan yakin akan diagnosis, beberapa pasien tidak merespons pengobatan pertama atau bahkan kedua yang tersedia. Itu tidak berarti diagnosis atau pengobatannya salah, melainkan orang bukanlah klon satu sama lain dan beberapa merespons lebih baik terhadap satu jenis pengobatan daripada yang lain.

    Mungkin suatu hari kita akan memiliki beberapa jenis tes genetik yang memberi tahu kita langsung obat atau rencana perawatan sempurna untuk suatu penyakit tertentu, tetapi hari itu tampaknya masih jauh.

    Satu hal terakhir yang perlu disebutkan adalah bahwa dokter yang baik tidak akan merasa terancam oleh pasien yang mengajukan pertanyaan atau melakukan penelitian. Ada kalanya seorang pasien akan menanyakan saya tentang pengobatan baru yang tidak saya kenal, dan saya perlu melakukan penelitian saya sendiri.

    Skenario-skenario itu bukan sesuatu yang mengganggu bagi saya melainkan kesempatan belajar. “Saya tidak akrab dengan itu,” akan saya katakan kepada pasien saya. “Biarkan saya melakukan sedikit penelitian dan berbicara dengan beberapa spesialis yang saya percayai, dan saya akan meneleponmu akhir minggu ini dan memberi tahu apa yang saya temukan.”

    Terkadang saya menyelidik dan menemukan bahwa pengobatan tersebut mahal dan tampaknya memberikan manfaat yang bercampur atau sedikit, tetapi terkadang itu merupakan perbaikan dibandingkan cara lama. Dokter perlu belajar dan menyesuaikan gaya praktik mereka seiring kita mempelajari hal baru tentang penyakit dan bagaimana tubuh manusia meresponsnya.

    Diperlukan Kerendahan Hati

    Semakin lama saya berdinas di dunia kedokteran, semakin sedikit saya merasa tahu. Bukan berarti saya mengalami demensia, tetapi lebih kepada saya menyadari bahwa ada banyak penyakit yang belum kita miliki pengobatan yang baik. Tubuh manusia sungguh luar biasa kompleks. Ada 36 triliun sel dalam tubuh manusia, dan biasanya, semuanya bekerja bersama dengan sempurna; masalahnya adalah mencari tahu apa yang harus dilakukan ketika mereka tidak.

    Efek Dunning-Kruger adalah sesuatu yang memengaruhi banyak bidang di mana orang dengan pengetahuan dan keterampilan terbatas secara signifikan melebih-lebihkan kemampuan mereka di bidang tersebut. Studi menunjukkan bahwa 65 persen orang Amerika percaya bahwa mereka memiliki IQ di atas rata-rata.4 Secara statistik, ini tidak mungkin. Lima puluh persen dari kelompok mana pun akan memiliki IQ di atas rata-rata, dan 50 persen lainnya akan berada di bawah rata-rata. Begitulah cara skala IQ disusun.

    Walaupun efek ini hadir pada dokter, itu juga hadir pada pasien. “Melakukan penelitianmu” tidak sama dengan menghabiskan empat tahun di Sekolah Kedokteran, tiga tahun lagi dalam program residensi, dan terus mengikuti perkembangan dalam kedokteran melalui berbagai kursus pendidikan. Kita semua akan baik-baik saja jika lebih banyak mendengarkan dan menyadari keterbatasan kita.

    Fakta bahwa sepupu ibu Anda mengonsumsi ekstrak milkweed dan merasa jauh lebih baik dari gejala yang mirip dengan Anda menarik. Apakah ekstrak milkweed membantu mereka sembuh dari penyakit mereka, apakah itu efek plasebo, atau apakah mereka memang akan sembuh sendirinya tanpa mempedulikan apa yang mereka konsumsi, itu masih menjadi perdebatan.

    Hikmat Sejati

    Saya telah menyebutkan hikmat sebelumnya, dan saya ingin menutup dengan itu. Hikmat sejati adalah menyadari bahwa kesembuhan berasal dari Allah. Mazmur 103:3 berkata tentang Allah, “Yang mengampuni segala kesalahanmu, yang menyembuhkan segala penyakitmu.”

    Penyembuhan tidak berasal dari antibiotik atau kemoterapi. Itu tidak berasal dari mengonsumsi suplemen yang tepat atau bahkan makan diet sehat. Penyembuhan terjadi karena Allah menyentuh kita, sampai bagian terkecil dari sel dan sistem kekebalan tubuh kita, dan membuat segala sesuatu menjadi utuh kembali.

    Saya percaya bahwa terkadang Dia bekerja melalui kedokteran, tetapi di lain waktu Dia bekerja melalui doa yang effektif dan bergelora dari orang-orang benar. (Yakobus 5:16)

    Dengan semua pengetahuan kita, mudah bagi kita menjadi sombong dan percaya bahwa kita tidak membutuhkan siapa pun lagi. Kita hidup di dunia yang dipenuhi pengetahuan dan sebuah dunia di mana hikmat telah mengambil tempat di belakang.

    Kita harus memilih sumber informasi kita dengan hati-hati dan menyadari bahwa kita tidak mengetahui segala sesuatu. Mungkin alasan mengapa takut akan Tuhan adalah permulaan hikmat adalah karena itu adalah langkah pertama bagi kita untuk meletakkan kesombongan kita dan menyadari bahwa kita hanyalah bagian kecil dari Sang Pencipta. Hanya kemudian, kita dapat dengan rendah hati mendengarkan, belajar, dan menerima penyembuhan.

The people we commonly refer to as the Russian Mennonites came into being as a group in a way quite similar to that of us with an Anabaptist heritage. We sprang from the same areas of Europe, from much of the same teachings of early Anabaptism, and have both experienced many of the same temptations and pitfalls, though at different times and locations.

This article will not focus on the beginnings of the Russian Mennonites apart from a brief overview. The group first entered Russia upon the urgings of the Viceroy Potemkin, who came into authority over the area now known as Ukraine after its annexation by Russia in 1783. The area had been under his partial administration since 1774, and he was eager to populate the land with foreign settlers. The residents of New Russia, as it was then called, were mostly nomads and Cossacks, a seminomadic group present in the steppes of Russia. The Mennonites in Danzig, Poland, were first approached with the offer of land, which would have appealed to them because they were routinely denied land ownership as a semi-persecuted people at that time. This offer came in August of 1786, and two brothers from the Danzig church were sent to survey the land and make arrangements for possible immigration.

The first immigration of 462 families began in 1788, and the “Old Colony” was established at Chortitza. They were afforded freedom of religion, exemption from military service, and the right to maintain their own schools and governances.

The Mennonites thrived in their new homeland. Although the first years were hard, partially due to the fact that mostly poorer families and those not in church leadership chose to resettle in Russia, the group soon began to transform the barren plains and steppes into rich agricultural communities. As the churches grew, so did their prosperity.

This period of relative peace lasted for over a century, until the late 1800s, when the Russian government, dissatisfied with the number of foreign settlements inside its borders, began applying pressure to many of the groups it had invited to settle its land some 100 years before. The Mennonites were not the only ones targeted, as many groups from various nations had established themselves in Russia. Steps taken against the Mennonites included pressure to participate in the armed forces as well as pressure to drop the German language that the communities had been using in favor of the Russian language. As these pressures increased, some Mennonites chose to flee the country in the 1870s. The majority, however, by now quite wealthy and affluent in comparison to their Russian peasant neighbors, chose to stay and weather the storm.

Unbeknownst to them, a full-scale revolution that would reshape Russia as a country was just around the corner. In 1917, the Bolsheviks came to power through the October Revolution, an event where the reigning tsar, or emperor, was deposed and exiled, and a new government was set up. A civil war broke out, and much of the fighting raged over the lands occupied by the Mennonites. Here, it is necessary to insert a brief history of the ideology of this new government.

The October Revolution and its subsequent change in government were fueled by a class war. As opposed to Nazi Germany, where a person could be arrested and killed for their race, in Russia, a person could and would be arrested for their class, for example, property ownership was seen as a crime against the people, and so the wealthier class of Russian peasants and farmers, those who most often owned property and employed the lower class of peasants, became an instant target a revolution that claimed to want to distribute all property and resources evenly amongst its citizenry.

By this time, the strong agricultural society of the Mennonites had transformed Ukraine into a breadbasket, its vast fields sown with wheat developed specifically by the Mennonites: Turkey Red Wheat. This hardy crop had made the Mennonite church quite wealthy, and their colonies had grown and flourished into villages of comfort and, at times, extravagance. This must have been a two-fold insult to the still impoverished peasants of Russia. Not only was there a large group of people in their midst that taught, spoke, and did their dealings in a language not of the Motherland, but these people also were wealthy beyond most peasants’ dreams.

It is, therefore, no surprise that when the kulaks, the wealthy class of peasants, came under persecution from the new government, the Mennonites were seen as the enemy of the people. As the civil war raged over Mennonite lands, villages were burnt and decimated, people executed or driven off, and livestock and grain plundered. Eventually, this period of fighting did come to an end, but for those few who survived the destruction, there was no reprieve to be found.

With the label of kulak and being generally defenseless, the Mennonites faced intense persecution. Religious services were rarely allowed, and the agricultural communities that had fed Russia and many others besides were collectivized and put under government control. Many of their churches ceased to exist entirely, although those in the east tended to last longer than the western villages.

Imagine then, to a people accustomed for generations to the favor and benevolence of material possessions and success, that all things material are stripped away. In a historical eye blink, the wealthy become the poor, and the favored become the hated. Even with a strong Christian faith, such a turn of events would shock and confuse.

But further tests were yet ahead for those who endured the first 25 years of the Soviet persecution. With the memory of their easy lives still fresh, the dawn of World War II brought a unique and enticing opportunity: the rise of a government that promoted the well-being of the German race, that valued those groups that could turn an empty prairie into a sprawling farm, that was vehemently anti-Communist- to this beleaguered group of believers, this must have seemed to be a God sent miracle to deliver them from their burdensome exile.

And so, they embraced the invading Germans. We readers, who are blessed with the ability to see the end result of these people’s decisions, can certainly make a good guess at what the end result was of wholesale support for the Nazis, but we must remember the scenarios that these Mennonites found themselves in...it was not one that would have been easy to decipher and decide upon if it were to be judged by man’s knowledge.

And so it was that the descendants of those helpless believers who gave their bodies at the stake and sword aligned themselves with a worldly kingdom that promised to protect and provide for them. In exchange for an eternal heritage, they chose to hope that the might of the German army would win back their earthly heritage and riches, and it was in this might that they trusted, forming bands of men who fought alongside the Germans against their old neighbors.

History did not deviate from its course, and the German army was eventually beaten back to its own borders and then further, and yet further into German lands. Before this retreating army ran those that had looked to it for their deliverance.

The atrocities of the Soviet government against its citizens are well documented in various works, most famously in the Gulag Archipelago, a book written by a Russian officer who was accused of treason. That author, Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn, painted a terrible picture of the treatment and exile of those who had opposed the USSR. Amongst the imprisoned or executed millions described in his tomes, there lie the remnants of a people who began as we did, experienced the smile of prosperity as we do, and then, treasuring that prosperity, lost it in calamitous fashion. We would do well to consider the paths we choose, as the wise king of the Scriptures instructs us, lest we, too, fall in the pursuit of prosperity. “Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established” (Proverbs 4:26).

Die mense wat ons algemeen as die Russiese Menoniete noem, het as ’n groep op ’n manier tot stand gekom wat baie soortgelyk is aan dié van ons met ’n Anabaptistiese erfenis. Ons het uit dieselfde gebiede van Europa ontstaan, uit baie van dieselfde leringe van die vroeë Anabaptisme, en ons het albei baie van dieselfde versoekings en slaggate ervaar, hoewel op verskillende tye en plekke.

Hierdie artikel sal nie op die begin van die Russiese Menoniete fokus nie, behalwe vir ’n kort oorsig. Die groep het eers Rusland binnegekom op versoek van die Visegraaf Potemkin, wat beheer oor die gebied wat nou as Oekraïne bekend staan gekry het ná die anneksasie deur Rusland in 1783. Die area was sedert 1774 onder sy gedeeltelike administrasie, en hy was gretig om die land met buitelandse setlaars te bevolk. Die inwoners van Nieu-Rusland, soos dit destyds genoem is, was meestal nomades en Kozakke, ’n semi-nomadiese groep wat in die steppe van Rusland teenwoordig was. Die Menoniete in Danzig, Pole, is eers genader met die aanbod van grond, wat vir hulle aantreklik sou wees omdat hulle daardie tyd gereeld verhoed is om grond te besit as ’n semi-vervolgde volk. Hierdie aanbod het in Augustus 1786 gekom, en twee broers van die Danzig-kerk is gestuur om die land te ondersoek en reëlings te tref vir moontlike immigrasie.

Die eerste immigrasie van 462 gesinne het in 1788 begin, en die “Oude Kolonie” is by Chortitza gestig. Hulle is vryheid van godsdiens, vrystelling van diens in die weermag, en die reg om hul eie skole en bestuursvorme te behou, toegestaan.

Die Menoniete het in hul nuwe tuisland gedy. Alhoewel die eerste jare moeilik was, deels omdat hoofsaaklik armer gesinne en dié wat nie in kerkleierskap was nie gekies het om na Rusland te herplaas, het die groep gou begin om die verlore vlaktes en steppe in ryk landbougemeenskappe te omskep. Namate die kerke gegroei het, het so ook hul welvaart.

Hierdie tydperk van relatiewe vrede het vir meer as ’n eeu geduur, tot laat 1800’s, toe die Russiese regering, ontevrede met die aantal buitelandse nedersettings binne sy grense, begin druk uitoefen op baie van die groepe wat die land ongeveer 100 jaar vroeër uitgenooi het om daar te kom woon. Die Menoniete was nie die enigstes wat geteiken is nie, aangesien baie groepe van verskeie nasies in Rusland gevestig het. Stappe teen die Menoniete het druk ingesluit om aan te sluit by die gewapende magte sowel as druk om die Duitse taal wat die gemeenskappe gebruik het te Laat vaar ten gunste van die Russiese taal. Namate hierdie druk toegeneem het, het sommige Menoniete in die 1870’s gekies om die land te verlaat. Die meerderheid, egter, wat teen hierdie tyd nogal ryk en welvarend was in vergelyking met hul Russiese boerbuurmanne, het gekies om te bly en die storm uit te staan.

Onbewus aan hulle was ’n volskaalse revolusie wat Rusland as ’n land sou hervorm, net om die hoek. In 1917 het die Bolsjewiste deur die Oktoberrevolusie aan bewind gekom, ’n gebeurtenis waar die heersende tsaar, of keiser, afgegradeer en verban is, en ’n nuwe regering ingestel is. ’n Burgeroorlog het uitgebreek, en baie van die gevegte het oor die lande gebrand waarvoor die Menoniete gewoon het. Hier is dit noodsaaklik om ’n kort geskiedenis van die ideologie van hierdie nuwe regering in te voeg.

Die Oktoberrevolusie en die daaropvolgende verandering in regering is aangedryf deur ’n klasoorlog. Anders as in Nazi-Duitsland, waar ’n persoon gearresteer en vermoor kon word vir hul ras, kon en sou ’n persoon in Rusland gearresteer word vir hul klas; byvoorbeeld eiendomsbesit is as ’n misdaad teen die volk beskou, en so het die rykere klas van Russiese boere en boerbesitters, dié wat dikwels eiendom besit en die laer klas boere in diens gehad het, ’n onmiddellike teiken van ’n revolusie geword wat beweer het dat dit alle eiendom en hulpbronne billik onder sy burgers wil verdeel.

Teen hierdie tyd het die sterk landbousamelewing van die Menoniete Oekraïne in ’n graanproduserende strook omskep, sy uitgestrekte lande ingeplant met koring spesifiek ontwikkel deur die Menoniete: Turkey Red-wes (Turkey Red Wheat). Hierdie taai gewas het die Menonitiese kerk nogal ryk gemaak, en hul kolonieë het gegroei en geblom in dorpe van gerief en soms weelde. Dit moes ’n dubbelslag-insult gewees het vir die nog steeds verarmde boere van Rusland. Nie net was daar ’n groot groep mense in hul midde wat in ’n taal gelei, gepraat en sake gedoen het wat nie die Moederland se taal was nie, maar hierdie mense was ook ryk bo meeste boere se drome uit.

Dit is dus geen verrassing dat toe die kulaks, die welgestelde klas boere, onder vervolging deur die nuwe regering gekom het, die Menoniete as die vyand van die volk gesien is nie. Terwyl die burgeroorlog oor Menonietlande woed, is dorpe afgebrand en verwoes, mense tereggestel of verdryf, en vee en graan geplunder. Uiteindelik het hierdie tydperk van gevegte tot ’n einde gekom, maar vir die weiniges wat die verwoesting oorleef het, was daar geen versagting te vind nie.

Met die etiket van kulak en algemeen ongeskik om hulself te verdedig, het die Menoniete intense vervolging in die gesig gestaar. Godsdienstige dienste is selde toegelaat, en die landbougemeenskappe wat Rusland en baie ander gevoed het, is gekollektiveer en onder staatsbeheer gestel. Baie van hul kerke het heeltemal opgehou bestaan, alhoewel dié in die ooste geneig was om langer te hou as die westelike dorpe.

Stel jou dus voor, aan ’n volk wat generasies lank gewoond was aan die guns en welwillendheid van materiële besittings en sukses, dat alle materiële dinge onttrek word. In ’n historiese oogwink word die rykes die armes, en die aangewesenes die gehates. Selfs met ’n sterk Christelike geloof sou so ’n ommekeer skok en verwarring veroorsaak.

Maar verdere beproewings was nog voorlê vir dié wat die eerste 25 jaar van die Sowjetvervolging deurstaan het. Met die herinnering aan hul maklike lewens nog vars, het die aanbreek van die Tweede Wêreldoorlog ’n unieke en aanloklike geleentheid gebring: die opkoms van ’n regering wat die welsyn van die Duitse ras bevorder het, wat daardie groepe waardeer het wat ’n leë prairie in ’n uitgestrekte plaas kon omskep, wat fel anti-Kommunisties was—vir hierdie geteisterde groep gelowiges moes dit ’n Godgesinde wonder gelyk het om hulle van hulle bloedige ballingskap te bevry.

En so het hulle die invalle Duitsers omhels. Ons lesers, wat die vermoë het om die eindresultaat van hierdie mense se besluite te sien, kan sekerlik ’n goeie raaiskoot maak oor wat die uitkoms was van massiewe ondersteuning vir die Natsionaliste, maar ons moet onthou die scenario’s waarin hierdie Menoniete hulself bevind het... dit was nie ’n situasie wat maklik te dekrypeer en te beslis sou wees as dit volgens menslike kennis beoordeel is nie.

En so het die nageslagte van daardie weerlose gelowiges wat hul liggame aan die stake en swaard gegee het, hulself verbind aan ’n wêreldse koninkryk wat belowe het om hulle te beskerm en vir hulle te voorsien. In ruil vir ’n ewige erfenis het hulle gekies om te hoop dat die mag van die Duitse leër hul aardse erfenis en rykdom sou herwin, en dit was op hierdie mag wat hulle vertrou het, met vorming van groepe mans wat langs die Duitsers geveg het teen hul ou bure.

Die geskiedenis het nie van koers verander nie, en die Duitse leër is uiteindelik teruggedring na sy eie grense en daarna verder, en steeds verder in Duitse gebiede. Voor hierdie terugtrekkende leër het diegene wat na hulle gekyk het vir hul verlossing, gevlug.

Die gruweldade van die Sowjetregering teen sy burgers is goed gedokumenteer in verskeie werke, die bekendste in die Gulag Archipelago, ’n boek geskryf deur ’n Russiese offisier wat van verraad beskuldig is. Daardie skrywer, Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn, het ’n verskriklike prentjie geskilder van die behandeling en ballingskap van dié wat die USSR teengestaan het. Tussen die gevangenes of tereggestelde miljoene wat in sy boeke beskryf word, lê die oorblyfsels van ’n volk wat begin het soos ons, die glimlag van welvaart ervaar het soos ons, en toe, dié welvaart koesterend, dit op ’n rampagtige wyse verloor het. Ons sou goed daaraan doen om die paaie wat ons kies, te oorweeg, soos die wyse koning van die Skrifte ons gebied, sodat ons nie ook val in die strewe na welvaart nie. “Bedink die gang van jou voete, en laat al jou paaie gevestig word” (Spreuke 4:26).

What do we think about when we think of the term ‘church’? We live in a day when there are many and varied churches. If one church doesn’t suit you, there are others to choose from. While some churches encourage their people to live for God and others instead of themselves, other churches promote a gospel that says lots of money and a better life now are the results of following Christ. However, there are still churches that try to follow what the Bible says—Sola scriptura (scripture alone). Traditionally, the conservative Anabaptist churches in America have tried to function in this manner. But is that changing?

We live in a day when lines are being crossed, blurred, and confused. People aren’t sure what is true and what is not. Today, men and women around the world are looking for answers and solutions, but where should they look?

I was talking with a young man who testified of being converted at a young age. He attended church faithfully and was considered quite gifted. But there was a problem—he had a sin that he still could not control. As he wrestled with God and pled for victory, he began to hear a recurring message from other professing Christians, “No one is perfect!” “We all have issues.” “Everyone has sinned!” Finally, this young man accepted his sin as normal. He justified it because it seemed that everyone was saying they had sin also, that they were not living in complete victory. It led this young man to a place of complete ruin.

Are we preaching and accepting a defeated Gospel—a gospel that doesn’t offer complete forgiveness and complete victory? Many youth of today are confused. Many people in today’s world don’t understand. Anyone can go to church and try to be a better person. But what about the all-powerful, life-changing gospel of Jesus Christ?

The apostle Paul says that Jesus is coming back for “. . .a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish” (Eph. 5:27). And Jesus Himself said “. . .That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it” (Matt. 16:18).

Before I was converted, I was certainly a slave to sin, but I wanted victory. I was addicted to drugs and alcohol, but I didn’t like it. I wanted to be free. I went to counseling and rehab facilities all over America, but it didn’t work. I had no power. I could quit for a few days or even weeks, then anger and depression would set in, and I would return to the substances. One day, I came face to face with the Creator. The hand of the almighty God got ahold of me and opened my eyes. I repented of my sins and was given a clean slate and a clean heart. I never went back. Drugs, alcohol, and two packs of cigarettes a day were finished—forever.

I could hardly believe what God was doing. The power of God was real. I could not overcome it by myself, as none of us can, but God has promised us freedom from bondage and a new life of victorious living if we submit our lives to him. This ability to overcome the power of sin and then walk in victory is what the world is looking for. Do we believe that God can free us not only from substance abuse but also from anger, selfishness, bitterness, greed, and pride? God’s Word says “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness” (1 John 1:9). No one is interested in a defeated Gospel, no one except those who are living in defeat because they have chosen the things of this world over God and His Word.

Are we willing to testify of the power of the resurrection? We need to proclaim a gospel that completely saves people from the bondage of sin—forever. We must be bold and confident in our faith so we can lead people to the Master.

I was witnessing to a man when he said in a rather loud voice, “God is not real!” My six-year-old son’s mouth fell open, and he gasped, “Daddy, he just told a lie!”

My son doesn’t need to be convinced that God is real; he believes it with all his heart. The world out there does need to be convinced. They need to see something that science cannot explain. They need to see something that defies all odds.

That something is a heart that has been truly changed. The fighter now loves his enemies. The person with an anger problem now loves others unconditionally. Broken families are healed. Wretched sinners are forgiven and living a transformed life. Hope, peace, love, and power are freely given to men and women who seemingly have no hope. “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them ” (Matt. 11:5).

Are you living your life so the world can see the work of God being practical, effective, and real every day? Here are a few things the Church needs in our day to once again draw in the lost.

A willingness to suffer

History would show that the church, all through the ages, has suffered for Christ. It was part of the cost of following Christ. The Bible says, “Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution” (2 Tim. 3:12). It was something that just happened.

Today, many people want the American dream. Folks live a good moral life, are good citizens, make a good living, and go to church on Sundays. But is that what we are called to? The gospel spread like wildfire when the church suffered persecution and did so willingly and joyfully. It was something the world had never seen—a faith that people showed by their life, and their death was something worth dying for. Let’s not be afraid to suffer for Christ today.

Denial of self

Then said Jesus unto his disciples, “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me” (Matt. 16:24).

Have you ever wondered why Jesus instructs us to deny ourselves? After all, He gave us desires and passions, so why must we deny them? I have heard people say that we need to align our will with God’s, but I do not find this in the Bible. Rather, we should simply deny our will and accept God’s will.

I remember the first day of boot camp when I joined the Marine Corps after graduating from high school. Close to one hundred young men were there. We all had our own desires and thoughts. We had our own identity. It was amazing to see all the diversity. It would have been a disaster if the United States of America had sent us off to battle that first day. So, they had a plan set in place to fix this problem. Over the next three months, they broke us. Physically and mentally, we learned how to deny ourselves and submit to our commanders and each other. The world is often amazed by the great discipline and unity for which the Marines are known.

When we become a part of the kingdom of God, we cannot be effective if we each do what we want. A body of believers can all have good intentions, but if any one person has not denied themselves, they will never be able to submit to the greater cause. There is a war raging, and we cannot fight it alone. We must deny ourselves, join forces with our brethren, and fight for victory in our homes, churches, and lives.

Submission

The Bible calls us to submit ourselves:

  • to God (Jas. 4:7).
  • [to those] that have the [spiritual] rule over you [us] (Heb. 13:17).
  • to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • one to another in the fear of God (Eph. 5:21).

Once we deny ourselves, then and only then, can we submit to others. Many people today have great difficulty in submitting to their fellow man. Some feel they are free in Christ; therefore, they can do as they please. There is a reason why we are instructed to submit to others. It is easy for us to drift away from sound doctrine when we believe we can figure everything out on our own.

When we have truly denied ourselves, we find that it is rather easy, and even a great blessing, to submit to the brotherhood. In fact, it is true freedom. What you want doesn’t matter, and you begin to depend on your brothers and sisters. When getting our own way isn’t important to us, then when we don’t get our way, we are fine with it. As we lay down our lives for each other, we become a force that the world doesn’t understand. The world was drawn to the church for centuries, wanting what it had. But amazingly, today, it seems the church is being drawn to the world, wanting what it has.

There is power in submission. Hundreds of years ago, a man named Alexander the Great conquered almost all of the then-known world using military strength and cleverness mixed with diplomacy.

The story is told that Alexander and a small company of soldiers approached a strongly fortified, walled city. Standing outside the walls, Alexander raised his voice and demanded to see the king. When the king arrived, Alexander insisted that the king surrender the city and its inhabitants to Alexander and his little band of fighting men.

The king laughed, “Why should I surrender to you? You can’t do us any harm!” So, Alexander offered to give the king a demonstration. He ordered his men to line up single file and start marching. He marched them straight toward a sheer cliff.

The townspeople gathered on the wall and watched in shocked silence as, one by one, Alexander’s soldiers marched, without hesitation, right off the cliff to their deaths! After ten soldiers died, Alexander ordered the rest of the men to return to his side. The townspeople and the king immediately surrendered to Alexander the Great. They realized that if a few men were actually willing to commit suicide at the command of this dynamic leader, then nothing could stop his eventual victory.

Obedience

Submission and obedience go hand in hand. If we are willing to submit to something or someone, we will want to obey it. It becomes very important to submit to those who are over us, especially the almighty God in Heaven. If we struggle to submit, we will usually struggle with obedience. God forbid if we begin to believe that we are better off doing things alone without our brothers.

Love

“By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another” (John 13:35).

People wave to each other at an intersection, or they will open the door for an elderly person. People are generally loving people until something doesn’t go their way. Then they can become very difficult. Is that the way the church today is showing its love to the world? As long as everything is going smoothly, and no one steps on our toes, we all get along and we love each other. Then as soon as there is something worth fighting over, we put the “boxing gloves” on. Doesn’t the Bible say that “charity (love) beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things” (1 Cor. 13:7)? True love is revealed when we face adversity or when a brother does something to offend us. That is the love that will show the world we are disciples of Jesus.

Do we love our brother enough to help when he is in need? Maybe he is unknowingly straying away from God in a certain area. How much do we love him? Some people think that love is only talking about positive things with each other, but if we truly love our brother, we will go to him in love and speak honestly with him. Then if we are practicing a lifestyle of denying ourselves and submitting to the brethren, it should go well. God forbid if we get angry with a brother who comes to us to show us our error.

When we have chosen to suffer with the people of God and have denied ourselves, then we appreciate when a brother or sister speaks into our lives. We will not allow ourselves to become offended.

Suffering for and with each other, plus denying ourselves for each other, often forms a solid love for one another. This type of love is the kind that the world around us does not know but desires greatly. The world is getting more selfish and independent as the days pass. We can’t afford to miss our opportunities to show them the power of God with our love for one another.

Godly people throughout the ages have had their opportunity to serve the King and spread the message of the Kingdom of God, but they have moved on to eternity. Today it is our turn. The fields are white unto harvest. Let’s plug in and, with God’s help, preserve the glorious church of Jesus Christ for our children, the next generation.

A cosa pensiamo quando pensiamo al termine «chiesa»? Viviamo in un tempo in cui ci sono chiese molteplici e varie. Se una chiesa non ti va bene, ce ne sono altre tra cui scegliere. Mentre alcune chiese esortano il loro popolo a vivere per Dio e per gli altri invece che per se stessi, altre promuovono un vangelo che afferma che molti soldi e una vita migliore ora sono il risultato del seguire Cristo. Tuttavia, ci sono ancora chiese che cercano di seguire ciò che dice la Bibbia—Sola scriptura (sola Scrittura). Tradizionalmente, le chiese anabattiste conservatrici in America hanno cercato di funzionare in questo modo. Ma sta cambiando?

Viviamo in un tempo in cui le linee vengono attraversate, sfumate e confuse. La gente non è sicura di ciò che è vero e di ciò che non lo è. Oggi, uomini e donne nel mondo cercano risposte e soluzioni, ma dove dovrebbero cercare?

Stavo parlando con un giovane che testimoniava di essere stato convertito in giovane età. Frequentava la chiesa fedelmente ed era considerato piuttosto dotato. Ma c’era un problema—aveva un peccato che non riusciva ancora a controllare. Mentre lottava con Dio e supplicava per la vittoria, cominciò a sentire un messaggio ricorrente da altri cristiani professanti: “Nessuno è perfetto!” “Tutti abbiamo problemi.” “Tutti hanno peccato!” Alla fine, questo giovane accettò il suo peccato come normale. Lo giustificò perché sembrava che tutti dicessero di avere peccati anch’essi, che non vivevano nella completa vittoria. Questo portò quel giovane in un luogo di rovina completa.

Stiamo predicando e accettando un Vangelo sconfitto—un vangelo che non offre perdono completo e vittoria completa? Molti giovani di oggi sono confusi. Molte persone nel mondo di oggi non capiscono. Chiunque può andare in chiesa e cercare di essere una persona migliore. Ma che dire del vangelo onnipotente che cambia la vita di Gesù Cristo?

L’apostolo Paolo dice che Gesù sta per tornare per «. . . una chiesa gloriosa, che non abbia macchia né rughe, né alcuna cosa simile; ma che sia santa e irreprensibile» (Eph. 5:27). E lo stesso Gesù disse «. . . Tu sei Pietro, e su questa pietra edificherò la mia chiesa; e le porte dell'inferno non prevarranno contro di essa» (Matt. 16:18).

Prima di essere convertito, ero certamente schiavo del peccato, ma volevo la vittoria. Ero dipendente da droghe e alcol, ma non mi piaceva. Volevo essere libero. Sono andato a consulenze e strutture di riabilitazione in tutta l’America, ma non ha funzionato. Non avevo potere. Potevo smettere per alcuni giorni o anche settimane, poi la rabbia e la depressione prendevano il sopravvento, e tornavo alle sostanze. Un giorno, mi trovai faccia a faccia col Creatore. La mano dell'Iddio onnipotente mi afferrò e mi aprì gli occhi. Mi pentii dei miei peccati e mi fu data una tabula rasa e un cuore nuovo. Non tornai mai indietro. Droghe, alcol e due pacchetti di sigarette al giorno finirono—per sempre.

Non potevo credere a quello che Dio stava facendo. Il potere di Dio era reale. Non potevo sconfiggerlo da solo, come nessuno di noi può, ma Dio ci ha promesso libertà dalla schiavitù e una nuova vita di vita vittoriosa se sottomettiamo le nostre vite a lui. Questa capacità di vincere il potere del peccato e poi camminare nella vittoria è ciò che il mondo sta cercando. Crediamo che Dio possa liberarci non solo dalla dipendenza da sostanze ma anche dalla rabbia, dall’egoismo, dall’amarezza, dall’avidità e dall’orgoglio? La Parola di Dio dice: «Se confessiamo i nostri peccati, egli è fedele e giusto da perdonarci i peccati e purificarci da ogni iniquità» (1 John 1:9). Nessuno è interessato a un Vangelo sconfitto, nessuno tranne coloro che vivono nella sconfitta perché hanno scelto le cose di questo mondo invece di Dio e della Sua Parola.

Siamo disposti a testimoniare il potere della risurrezione? Dobbiamo proclamare un vangelo che salvi completamente le persone dalla schiavitù del peccato—per sempre. Dobbiamo essere audaci e fiduciosi nella nostra fede così da poter condurre le persone al Maestro.

Stavo testimoniando a un uomo quando egli disse a voce abbastanza alta: “Dio non è reale!” La bocca del mio figlio di sei anni si spalancò, ed esclamò, “Papà, ha appena detto una bugia!”

Mio figlio non ha bisogno di essere convinto che Dio è reale; ci crede con tutto il cuore. Il mondo là fuori ha bisogno di essere convinto. Hanno bisogno di vedere qualcosa che la scienza non può spiegare. Hanno bisogno di vedere qualcosa che sfida ogni probabilità.

Quella cosa è un cuore che è stato veramente cambiato. Il combattente ora ama i suoi nemici. La persona con un problema di rabbia ora ama gli altri incondizionatamente. Famiglie spezzate vengono guarite. Miserabili peccatori sono perdonati e vivono una vita trasformata. Speranza, pace, amore e potere sono donati gratuitamente a uomini e donne che apparentemente non hanno speranza. «I ciechi riacquistano la vista, e gli zoppi camminano, i lebbrosi sono purificati, e i sordi odono, i morti sono risuscitati, e ai poveri è predicato il vangelo» (Matt. 11:5).

Stai vivendo la tua vita affinché il mondo possa vedere l’opera di Dio pratica, efficace e reale ogni giorno? Ecco alcune cose di cui la Chiesa ha bisogno nel nostro tempo per attrarre nuovamente i perduti.

Una disponibilità a soffrire

La storia mostrerebbe che la chiesa, attraverso i secoli, ha sofferto per Cristo. Era parte del costo del seguire Cristo. La Bibbia dice: «Sì, e tutti quelli che vogliono vivere piamente in Cristo Gesù saranno perseguitati» (2 Tim. 3:12). Era qualcosa che accadeva naturalmente.

Oggi, molte persone vogliono il sogno americano. La gente vive una buona vita morale, è brava cittadina, guadagna bene e va in chiesa la domenica. Ma è questo ciò a cui siamo chiamati? Il vangelo si diffuse come incendio quando la chiesa subì persecuzione e lo fece volontariamente e gioiosamente. Era qualcosa che il mondo non aveva mai visto—una fede che la gente mostrava con la propria vita, e la loro morte era qualcosa per cui valeva la pena morire. Non temiamo di soffrire per Cristo oggi.

Negazione di sé

Allora Gesù disse ai suoi discepoli: «Se qualcuno vuole venire dopo di me, rinneghi se stesso, prenda la sua croce e mi segua» (Matt. 16:24).

Ti sei mai chiesto perché Gesù ci istruisce a rinnegarci? Dopotutto, Egli ci ha dato desideri e passioni, quindi perché dobbiamo rinnegarli? Ho sentito persone dire che dobbiamo allineare la nostra volontà con quella di Dio, ma non trovo questo nella Bibbia. Piuttosto, dovremmo semplicemente rinnegare la nostra volontà e accettare la volontà di Dio.

Ricordo il primo giorno di addestramento quando mi arruolai nei Marine Corps dopo il diploma di scuola superiore. Eravamo vicino a cento giovani uomini lì. Ognuno di noi aveva i propri desideri e pensieri. Avevamo la nostra identità. Era sorprendente vedere tutta quella diversità. Sarebbe stato un disastro se gli Stati Uniti d'America ci avessero mandato in battaglia quel primo giorno. Così, avevano un piano per risolvere questo problema. Nei successivi tre mesi, ci hanno spezzati. Fisicamente e mentalmente, abbiamo imparato a rinnegarci e a sottometterci ai nostri comandanti e gli uni agli altri. Il mondo è spesso stupito dalla grande disciplina e unità per cui i Marines sono conosciuti.

Quando entriamo a far parte del regno di Dio, non possiamo essere efficaci se ciascuno di noi fa ciò che vuole. Un corpo di credenti può avere tutte buone intenzioni, ma se anche una sola persona non si è rinnegata, non sarà mai in grado di sottomettersi alla causa più grande. C’è una guerra in corso, e non possiamo combatterla da soli. Dobbiamo rinnegarci, unirci alle forze dei nostri fratelli e combattere per la vittoria nelle nostre case, chiese e vite.

Sottomissione

La Bibbia ci chiama a sottometterci:

  • a Dio (Jas. 4:7).
  • [a coloro] che hanno la [guida spirituale] su di voi [noi] (Heb. 13:17).
  • ad ogni ordinanza dell'uomo per amor del Signore (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • l'uno all'altro nel timore di Dio (Eph. 5:21).

Una volta che ci rinneghiamo, allora e solo allora, possiamo sottometterci agli altri. Molte persone oggi hanno grande difficoltà a sottomettersi al loro prossimo. Alcuni sentono di essere liberi in Cristo; perciò, possono fare come gli pare. C’è una ragione per cui ci è comandato di sottometterci agli altri. È facile per noi allontanarci dalla sana dottrina quando crediamo di poter capire tutto da soli.

Quando ci siamo veramente rinnegati, scopriamo che è piuttosto facile, e persino una grande benedizione, sottometterci alla fratellanza. In effetti, è vera libertà. Ciò che vuoi non importa, e cominci a dipendere dai tuoi fratelli e sorelle. Quando ottenere ciò che vogliamo non è importante per noi, allora quando non lo otteniamo, stiamo bene lo stesso. Mentre ci doniamo l'un l'altro, diventiamo una forza che il mondo non capisce. Il mondo è stato attratto dalla chiesa per secoli, desiderando ciò che essa aveva. Ma sorprendentemente, oggi sembra che la chiesa sia attratta dal mondo, desiderando ciò che esso ha.

C’è potere nella sottomissione. Centinaia di anni fa, un uomo di nome Alessandro Magno conquistò quasi tutto il mondo allora conosciuto usando forza militare e astuzia mescolate con diplomazia.

Si racconta che Alessandro e una piccola compagnia di soldati si avvicinarono a una città fortificata e murata. Stando fuori dalle mura, Alessandro alzò la voce e chiese di vedere il re. Quando il re arrivò, Alessandro insistette che il re si arrendesse la città e i suoi abitanti a lui e alla sua piccola schiera di soldati.

Il re rise: «Perché dovrei arrendermi a te? Non puoi farci del male!» Così, Alessandro offrì al re una dimostrazione. Ordinò ai suoi uomini di mettersi in fila e cominciare a marciare. Li fece marciare dritti verso una parete a picco.

La gente della città si radunò sulla mura e osservò in silenzio scioccato mentre, uno dopo l'altro, i soldati di Alessandro marciavano, senza esitazione, proprio giù dalla scogliera verso la morte! Dopo che dieci soldati morirono, Alessandro ordinò al resto degli uomini di tornare al suo fianco. La gente della città e il re si arresero immediatamente ad Alessandro Magno. Si resero conto che se pochi uomini erano davvero disposti a commettere suicidio al comando di quel leader dinamico, allora nulla avrebbe potuto fermare la sua vittoria eventuale.

Obbedienza

Sottomissione e obbedienza vanno di pari passo. Se siamo disposti a sottometterci a qualcosa o a qualcuno, vorrremo obbedirgli. Diventa molto importante sottomettersi a coloro che stanno sopra di noi, specialmente all'Iddio onnipotente in Cielo. Se lottiamo per sottometterci, di solito lotteremo con l'obbedienza. Dio ce ne scampi se cominciamo a credere che sia meglio fare le cose da soli senza i nostri fratelli.

Amore

«Da questo conosceranno tutti che siete miei discepoli: se avrete amore gli uni per gli altri» (John 13:35).

Le persone si salutano con la mano a un incrocio, o aprono la porta a una persona anziana. Le persone sono generalmente amabili finché qualcosa non va per il loro verso. Poi possono diventare molto difficili. È questo il modo in cui la chiesa oggi mostra il suo amore al mondo? Finché tutto procede senza intoppi, e nessuno calpesta i nostri piedi, andiamo tutti d'accordo e ci amiamo. Poi non appena c'è qualcosa per cui vale la pena lottare, mettiamo i «guantoni da boxe». Non dice la Bibbia che «la carità (amore) tutto copre, tutto crede, tutto spera, tutto sopporta» (1 Cor. 13:7)? Il vero amore si rivela quando affrontiamo l'avversità o quando un fratello fa qualcosa per offenderci. Quell'amore è ciò che mostrerà al mondo che siamo discepoli di Gesù.

Amiamo abbastanza il nostro fratello da aiutarlo quando è nel bisogno? Forse sta inconsapevolmente allontanandosi da Dio in un certo ambito. Quanto lo amiamo? Alcune persone pensano che l'amore significhi parlare solo di cose positive tra di noi, ma se amiamo veramente il nostro fratello, andremo da lui con amore e gli parleremo onestamente. Allora se pratichiamo uno stile di vita di rinnegamento di noi stessi e sottomissione ai fratelli, dovrebbe andare bene. Dio ce ne scampi se ci arrabbiamo con un fratello che viene da noi per mostrarci il nostro errore.

Quando abbiamo scelto di soffrire con il popolo di Dio e ci siamo rinnegati, apprezziamo quando un fratello o una sorella interviene nelle nostre vite. Non permetteremo di essere offesi facilmente.

Soffrire per e con gli altri, oltre a rinnegarci per gli altri, spesso forma un amore solido l'uno per l'altro. Questo tipo di amore è quello che il mondo intorno a noi non conosce ma desidera fortemente. Il mondo diventa sempre più egoista e indipendente con il passare dei giorni. Non possiamo permetterci di perdere le nostre opportunità di mostrare loro il potere di Dio con il nostro amore reciproco.

Persone pii attraverso i secoli hanno avuto la loro opportunità di servire il Re e diffondere il messaggio del Regno di Dio, ma sono passate all'eternità. Oggi tocca a noi. I campi sono già bianchi per la mietitura. Impegniamoci e, con l'aiuto di Dio, preserviamo la gloriosa chiesa di Gesù Cristo per i nostri figli, la prossima generazione.

What do we think about when we think of the term ‘church’? We live in a day when there are many and varied churches. If one church doesn’t suit you, there are others to choose from. While some churches encourage their people to live for God and others instead of themselves, other churches promote a gospel that says lots of money and a better life now are the results of following Christ. However, there are still churches that try to follow what the Bible says—Sola scriptura (scripture alone). Traditionally, the conservative Anabaptist churches in America have tried to function in this manner. But is that changing?

We live in a day when lines are being crossed, blurred, and confused. People aren’t sure what is true and what is not. Today, men and women around the world are looking for answers and solutions, but where should they look?

I was talking with a young man who testified of being converted at a young age. He attended church faithfully and was considered quite gifted. But there was a problem—he had a sin that he still could not control. As he wrestled with God and pled for victory, he began to hear a recurring message from other professing Christians, “No one is perfect!” “We all have issues.” “Everyone has sinned!” Finally, this young man accepted his sin as normal. He justified it because it seemed that everyone was saying they had sin also, that they were not living in complete victory. It led this young man to a place of complete ruin.

Are we preaching and accepting a defeated Gospel—a gospel that doesn’t offer complete forgiveness and complete victory? Many youth of today are confused. Many people in today’s world don’t understand. Anyone can go to church and try to be a better person. But what about the all-powerful, life-changing gospel of Jesus Christ?

The apostle Paul says that Jesus is coming back for “. . .a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish” (Eph. 5:27). And Jesus Himself said “. . .That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it” (Matt. 16:18).

Before I was converted, I was certainly a slave to sin, but I wanted victory. I was addicted to drugs and alcohol, but I didn’t like it. I wanted to be free. I went to counseling and rehab facilities all over America, but it didn’t work. I had no power. I could quit for a few days or even weeks, then anger and depression would set in, and I would return to the substances. One day, I came face to face with the Creator. The hand of the almighty God got ahold of me and opened my eyes. I repented of my sins and was given a clean slate and a clean heart. I never went back. Drugs, alcohol, and two packs of cigarettes a day were finished—forever.

I could hardly believe what God was doing. The power of God was real. I could not overcome it by myself, as none of us can, but God has promised us freedom from bondage and a new life of victorious living if we submit our lives to him. This ability to overcome the power of sin and then walk in victory is what the world is looking for. Do we believe that God can free us not only from substance abuse but also from anger, selfishness, bitterness, greed, and pride? God’s Word says “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness” (1 John 1:9). No one is interested in a defeated Gospel, no one except those who are living in defeat because they have chosen the things of this world over God and His Word.

Are we willing to testify of the power of the resurrection? We need to proclaim a gospel that completely saves people from the bondage of sin—forever. We must be bold and confident in our faith so we can lead people to the Master.

I was witnessing to a man when he said in a rather loud voice, “God is not real!” My six-year-old son’s mouth fell open, and he gasped, “Daddy, he just told a lie!”

My son doesn’t need to be convinced that God is real; he believes it with all his heart. The world out there does need to be convinced. They need to see something that science cannot explain. They need to see something that defies all odds.

That something is a heart that has been truly changed. The fighter now loves his enemies. The person with an anger problem now loves others unconditionally. Broken families are healed. Wretched sinners are forgiven and living a transformed life. Hope, peace, love, and power are freely given to men and women who seemingly have no hope. “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them ” (Matt. 11:5).

Are you living your life so the world can see the work of God being practical, effective, and real every day? Here are a few things the Church needs in our day to once again draw in the lost.

A willingness to suffer

History would show that the church, all through the ages, has suffered for Christ. It was part of the cost of following Christ. The Bible says, “Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution” (2 Tim. 3:12). It was something that just happened.

Today, many people want the American dream. Folks live a good moral life, are good citizens, make a good living, and go to church on Sundays. But is that what we are called to? The gospel spread like wildfire when the church suffered persecution and did so willingly and joyfully. It was something the world had never seen—a faith that people showed by their life, and their death was something worth dying for. Let’s not be afraid to suffer for Christ today.

Denial of self

Then said Jesus unto his disciples, “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me” (Matt. 16:24).

Have you ever wondered why Jesus instructs us to deny ourselves? After all, He gave us desires and passions, so why must we deny them? I have heard people say that we need to align our will with God’s, but I do not find this in the Bible. Rather, we should simply deny our will and accept God’s will.

I remember the first day of boot camp when I joined the Marine Corps after graduating from high school. Close to one hundred young men were there. We all had our own desires and thoughts. We had our own identity. It was amazing to see all the diversity. It would have been a disaster if the United States of America had sent us off to battle that first day. So, they had a plan set in place to fix this problem. Over the next three months, they broke us. Physically and mentally, we learned how to deny ourselves and submit to our commanders and each other. The world is often amazed by the great discipline and unity for which the Marines are known.

When we become a part of the kingdom of God, we cannot be effective if we each do what we want. A body of believers can all have good intentions, but if any one person has not denied themselves, they will never be able to submit to the greater cause. There is a war raging, and we cannot fight it alone. We must deny ourselves, join forces with our brethren, and fight for victory in our homes, churches, and lives.

Submission

The Bible calls us to submit ourselves:

  • to God (Jas. 4:7).
  • [to those] that have the [spiritual] rule over you [us] (Heb. 13:17).
  • to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • one to another in the fear of God (Eph. 5:21).

Once we deny ourselves, then and only then, can we submit to others. Many people today have great difficulty in submitting to their fellow man. Some feel they are free in Christ; therefore, they can do as they please. There is a reason why we are instructed to submit to others. It is easy for us to drift away from sound doctrine when we believe we can figure everything out on our own.

When we have truly denied ourselves, we find that it is rather easy, and even a great blessing, to submit to the brotherhood. In fact, it is true freedom. What you want doesn’t matter, and you begin to depend on your brothers and sisters. When getting our own way isn’t important to us, then when we don’t get our way, we are fine with it. As we lay down our lives for each other, we become a force that the world doesn’t understand. The world was drawn to the church for centuries, wanting what it had. But amazingly, today, it seems the church is being drawn to the world, wanting what it has.

There is power in submission. Hundreds of years ago, a man named Alexander the Great conquered almost all of the then-known world using military strength and cleverness mixed with diplomacy.

The story is told that Alexander and a small company of soldiers approached a strongly fortified, walled city. Standing outside the walls, Alexander raised his voice and demanded to see the king. When the king arrived, Alexander insisted that the king surrender the city and its inhabitants to Alexander and his little band of fighting men.

The king laughed, “Why should I surrender to you? You can’t do us any harm!” So, Alexander offered to give the king a demonstration. He ordered his men to line up single file and start marching. He marched them straight toward a sheer cliff.

The townspeople gathered on the wall and watched in shocked silence as, one by one, Alexander’s soldiers marched, without hesitation, right off the cliff to their deaths! After ten soldiers died, Alexander ordered the rest of the men to return to his side. The townspeople and the king immediately surrendered to Alexander the Great. They realized that if a few men were actually willing to commit suicide at the command of this dynamic leader, then nothing could stop his eventual victory.

Obedience

Submission and obedience go hand in hand. If we are willing to submit to something or someone, we will want to obey it. It becomes very important to submit to those who are over us, especially the almighty God in Heaven. If we struggle to submit, we will usually struggle with obedience. God forbid if we begin to believe that we are better off doing things alone without our brothers.

Love

“By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another” (John 13:35).

People wave to each other at an intersection, or they will open the door for an elderly person. People are generally loving people until something doesn’t go their way. Then they can become very difficult. Is that the way the church today is showing its love to the world? As long as everything is going smoothly, and no one steps on our toes, we all get along and we love each other. Then as soon as there is something worth fighting over, we put the “boxing gloves” on. Doesn’t the Bible say that “charity (love) beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things” (1 Cor. 13:7)? True love is revealed when we face adversity or when a brother does something to offend us. That is the love that will show the world we are disciples of Jesus.

Do we love our brother enough to help when he is in need? Maybe he is unknowingly straying away from God in a certain area. How much do we love him? Some people think that love is only talking about positive things with each other, but if we truly love our brother, we will go to him in love and speak honestly with him. Then if we are practicing a lifestyle of denying ourselves and submitting to the brethren, it should go well. God forbid if we get angry with a brother who comes to us to show us our error.

When we have chosen to suffer with the people of God and have denied ourselves, then we appreciate when a brother or sister speaks into our lives. We will not allow ourselves to become offended.

Suffering for and with each other, plus denying ourselves for each other, often forms a solid love for one another. This type of love is the kind that the world around us does not know but desires greatly. The world is getting more selfish and independent as the days pass. We can’t afford to miss our opportunities to show them the power of God with our love for one another.

Godly people throughout the ages have had their opportunity to serve the King and spread the message of the Kingdom of God, but they have moved on to eternity. Today it is our turn. The fields are white unto harvest. Let’s plug in and, with God’s help, preserve the glorious church of Jesus Christ for our children, the next generation.
