“Dus, wat brengt u hier vandaag?” vroeg ik aan Ben, een 40-jarige man die tegenover me zat.

“Nou,” antwoordde hij. “Ik heb een paar verschillende klachten. De grootste is dat ik altijd moe ben, maar ik ben ook aangekomen en mijn knieën doen ’s ochtends wat pijn.”

In mijn hoofd begon ik met wat artsen een differentiële diagnose noemen – de dingen die een cluster van symptomen kunnen veroorzaken die een patiënt heeft. Meestal laat ik de patiënt uitleggen welke klachten hij ervaart en stel ik daarna vragen om te proberen de specifieke diagnose te verfijnen.

Ben praatte nog even door. Toen haalde hij een stuk papier tevoorschijn. “Dus, dokter,” zei hij tegen me. “Ik heb wat onderzoek gedaan naar mijn diagnose, en ik denk dat dit tests zijn die ik nodig heb om het uit te zoeken.”

Ik keek naar de lijst. Die was behoorlijk lang en bevatte enkele dingen die ik waarschijnlijk toch had aangevraagd, zoals een bloedbeeld en een schildklierwaarde, maar ook wat heel vreemde dingen zoals een vitamine B1-waarde en een DHEA-waarde. Hij wilde ook een CT-scan van zijn hoofd, borst en buik.

“Dat is veel onderzoek,” zei ik. “Ik weet niet zeker of we alles hoeven te doen. Kunnen we nog wat meer praten over uw klachten en dan proberen te bepalen welke tests het beste zijn om het uit te zoeken?”

Ben was niet onder de indruk. “Ik heb mijn onderzoek gedaan!” zei hij vastberaden. “Tegenwoordig kun je met internet dingen vinden die je dokter je niet zou vertellen – misschien dingen waar hij zelfs niet aan denkt om te testen. Het probleem is dat IK U nodig heb om deze dingen voor mij aan te vragen zodat mijn verzekering ze vergoedt. Anders was ik hier niet eens geweest.”

We laten Ben en zijn ongemakkelijke dokter hierbij achter. Er zijn altijd patiënten geweest die artikelen uit tijdschriften meebrachten met titels als “Zes dingen die uw dokter u niet zal vertellen over uw gezondheid” en een lijst met tests die gedaan zouden moeten worden. Het lijkt erger te zijn geworden.

Veel patiënten weten meer dan hun dokters. Ze kunnen hun symptomen op het web opzoeken en allerlei oorzaken voor die klachten vinden.

Bovendien is kunstmatige intelligentie slim. ChatGPT, een platform voor kunstmatige intelligentie, slaagde voor de drie onderdelen van het Amerikaanse examen voor medische bevoegdheid.1 Het deed het niet geweldig — het haalde net iets boven een voldoende — maar ik veronderstel dat dat goed genoeg is om een praktijk tegenover de mijne te openen en patiënten te gaan zien.

Op sommige manieren is het goed dat patiënten toegang hebben tot dit niveau van informatie. Dokters zijn geen soort hogepriesters die speciale rechten hebben om het Heiligste der Heiligen van medische informatie te betreden. Bovendien zijn dokters verre van perfect, en je hoeft maar online recensies te lezen om te zien dat ze niet goed luisteren, procedures verknoeien en worstelen met moeilijke diagnoses.

Het kan echter lastig zijn wanneer patiënten geloven dat zij meer weten dan hun dokter. Ik heb altijd gezegd dat als je meer weet dan je dokter, je ofwel een flinke dosis nederigheid nodig hebt of een nieuwe dokter — of misschien allebei.

Verwerf wijsheid!

Prediker 4:5-9 zegt: “Verwerf wijsheid, verwerf inzicht; vergeet het niet en wijk niet af van de woorden van mijn mond. Verlaat haar niet, dan zal zij u bewaren; heb haar lief, dan zal zij u behoeden. Wijsheid is het voornaamste; verkrijg dan wijsheid, en met al uw verkrijging verkrijg inzicht. Verhef haar, dan zal zij u verhogen; zij zal u eren, wanneer u haar omhelst. Zij zal een krans van genade geven aan uw hoofd; een kroon van majesteit zal zij u schenken.”

Spreuken 18:15 spreekt over het verwerven van kennis, maar het geeft aan dat voordat we kennis zoeken, we ervoor moeten zorgen dat we wijsheid en inzicht hebben.

De auteur van het boek Spreuken was Salomo. We weten dat hij vroeg in zijn regering een droom had waarin God tot hem verscheen en hem aanbood wat hij maar begeerde. In zijn nederigheid vroeg Salomo om een begrijpend hart, zodat hij een groot volk wijs zou kunnen leiden (I Koningen 3:9,10).

Als we naar kennis kijken, is het eenvoudigweg een verzameling feiten — informatieblokjes die moeten worden samengevoegd tot een samenhangend geheel. Wijsheid en inzicht zijn de gereedschappen waarmee we de kennis die we hebben verworven betekenis geven.

Wijsheid laat ons ook de nauwkeurigheid van de bronnen van “kennis” oordelen. Het helpt ons de vraag te stellen: “Probeert deze persoon mij iets te verkopen? Heeft hij werkelijk wetenschappelijke studies die aantonen dat wat hij zegt waar is?”

Dit zijn twee vragen die ik stel als ik een website bekijk. Zijn er links naar producten die mij worden verkocht, en is de reclame duidelijk gescheiden van de artikelen? Bovendien, zijn er links naar studies die ondersteunen wat wordt beweerd? En zo ja, hoe groot waren die studies? Als een studie slechts 12 personen omvat, is die niet groot genoeg om betrouwbare informatie te leveren.

Robert Harris maakte het acroniem CARS, dat helpt bepalen of informatie op een website geldig is. Credibility (geloofwaardigheid), Accuracy (voorgaande nauwkeurigheid), Reasonableness (redelijkheid) en Supporting information (ondersteunende informatie) zijn allemaal belangrijk om te bekijken om te beoordelen of we waarde moeten hechten aan de informatie op een website.2

Helaas proberen veel mensen die beweren de antwoorden te hebben voor een lang en gezond leven eigenlijk boeken, supplementen en allerlei andere producten te verkopen. Een vooraanstaande arts die betere gezondheid promoot door het gebruik van supplementen (die hij verkoopt) heeft door dat proces genoeg geld vergaard dat hij in een verklaring in 2017 stelde dat hij meer dan 100 miljoen dollar waard was. Dat betekent niet dat hij niets te bieden heeft, maar het zegt wel dat hij een bias heeft ten gunste van het aanbevelen van dingen die hij verkoopt.

De American Medical Association heeft richtlijnen voor artsen om ethisch producten vanuit hun praktijk te verkopen. Die richtlijnen zeggen dat de producten een dringende behoefte moeten vervullen (bijvoorbeeld krukken bij een orthopedische praktijk), wetenschappelijke geldigheid voor hun gebruik moeten hebben, en dat artsen informatie moeten geven over andere manieren waarop patiënten dezelfde producten elders kunnen verkrijgen.3 Bovendien moeten artsen hun patiënten elke financiële belang onthullen die zij hebben in het product dat aan de patiënt wordt aangeboden.

Bevestigingsbias

De meesten van ons lezen om de dingen te bevestigen die we al geloven. Ik zie dit wanneer mensen de Bijbel lezen — op de een of andere manier kunnen mensen de Bijbel lezen en Schriftplaatsen die hun gedrag tegenspreken op het gebied van politieke betrokkenheid of bescheiden kleding compleet negeren, maar toch geloven dat ze alles volgens de Schrift volgen.

Op dezelfde manier kan ieder van ons verhalen en informatie vinden die onze opvattingen over dokters en geneeskunde bevestigen. Als we geloven dat dokters alleen uit zijn op geld en onethisch zijn en medicijnen voorschrijven die toxisch zijn voor patiënten, kunnen we artikelen vinden die dat bevestigen. Aan de andere kant, als we zoeken naar verhalen die alternatieve geneeskunde afkraken, kunnen we ook die artikelen vinden.

Het belangrijke is dat we de kwestie benaderen op zoek naar echte antwoorden en begrijpen dat de wetenschap niet alles weet.

Als voorbeeld: we hebben geen goede behandelingen voor mensen met Langdurige COVID-klachten. Dat betekent niet dat veel mensen die COVID hebben doorgemaakt maanden later niet lijden aan dingen zoals mentale mist en vermoeidheid, maar het betekent wel dat er geen enkel medicijn is dat in onderzoeken beter presteerde dan placebo’s om die symptomen te laten verdwijnen.

Bij gebrek aan wetenschappelijk bewezen behandelplannen hebben veel klinieken hun eigen behandeltrajecten ontwikkeld, met een mix van supplementen en zelfs hyperbare zuurstoftherapieën. Zijn die nuttig? Ik weet het niet, maar ik weet wel dat degenen die ze op de markt brengen vol vertrouwen zullen beweren dat ze een buitengewoon hoog slagingspercentage hebben in het genezen van mensen als ze gewoon bereid zijn het behandelingsplan te volgen (en ervoor te betalen).

Bovendien, wanneer mensen hun symptomen onderzoeken, neigen ze diagnoses te kiezen die zij waarschijnlijk achten op basis van hun onderliggende persoonlijkheidstypes. Sommige mensen zijn geneigd te catastrophiseren — dat wil zeggen, ze geloven onmiddellijk het slechtst denkbare resultaat van elk gegeven scenario. Deze mensen typen hun symptomen in en komen tot de conclusie dat ze kanker hebben en nog maar dagen of weken te leven hebben. Zoals God tegen Hizkia zei, is het tijd voor hen om hun huis op orde te brengen.

Aan de andere kant zijn er genoeg mensen met een optimistische persoonlijkheid. Zij typen hun lijst met klachten in en concluderen dat ze een milde virale aandoening hebben en zich over een paar dagen beter zullen voelen.

Het hele punt van het hebben van een zorgverlener is dat de behandelaar (hopelijk) de waarschijnlijke zaken van de onwaarschijnlijke kan scheiden. Zij hebben niet de emotionele overspanning die patiënten hebben, zodat ze objectief kunnen beslissen hoeveel testen te bestellen en welk type testen om tot een diagnose te komen.

Dokters kunnen gevaarlijke situaties herkennen

Ik herinner me dat ik jaren geleden een patiënte zag die bij me kwam met wat zij dacht dat een sinusinfectie was. Ze was in de twintig en zei dat ze een bonzend gevoel in haar hoofd had en veel druk.

Ze had eigenlijk geen afscheiding of koorts en geen van de typische symptomen van een sinusinfectie, maar sinusitis leek de meest waarschijnlijke diagnose die zij kon bedenken.

Ik keek haar één keer aan en ik vond het niet goed. Ten eerste was ze extreem bleek. Ten tweede was haar hartslag behoorlijk snel – 130 slagen per minuut in rust. Bij onderzoek vond ik niets dat aangaf dat ze een sinusinfectie had.

“Jenny,” zei ik tegen haar. “Ik heb je nodig om naar het ziekenhuis te gaan en acuut een volledig bloedbeeld te laten doen. Ik ben bang dat je echt anemisch bent — hoewel ik niet weet waardoor. Wacht bij het laboratorium en ik zal met je praten zodra ik de uitslagen heb.”

Ongeveer twintig minuten later kreeg ik wellicht een dringende oproep van het ziekenhuislaboratorium. “Dr. Waldron,” zei de stem aan de andere kant. “We hebben een kritieke laboratoriumuitslag voor u…”

Jenny’s hemoglobine was 4,6 (normaal is tussen 12 en 16), en ze kreeg uiteindelijk een transfusie. Wat ze niet kreeg, was behandeling voor een sinusinfectie.

Pijn op de borst is een klassiek symptoom dat kan wijzen op een onderliggende hartaandoening. Tegelijkertijd kan het gewoon wijzen op reflux (zuur in de slokdarm) of ontsteking in een rib of spier. Ik zie waarschijnlijk een paar patiënten per dag met deze klacht.

De meerderheid van hen heeft een eenvoudige behandeling nodig, maar een paar van hen moeten met spoed naar het ziekenhuis worden doorverwezen voor een volledige hartaandoeningsevaluatie. Ik weet niet hoe een online zoekmachine kan weten welke richting iemand op moet na het beoordelen van hun symptomen.

In het beste geval zal een online bron een gebruiker verwijzen naar spoedeisende hulp of hun lokale arts.

Niet alle dokters zijn gelijk

Ongeveer 50 procent van de dokters eindigde in de onderste helft van hun klas op de medische school. Alleen omdat iemand geen topcijfers had op de medische school, betekent dat niet dat hij geen adequate kennis heeft om een kwaal te behandelen. Misschien is de belangrijkste kennis die een dokter nodig heeft te weten wanneer hij het niet weet.

Het blijft moeilijk voor patiënten om te weten of ze te maken hebben met iemand die hen zal helpen. Wanneer je een dokter ontmoet, beoordeel je hem vaak op zijn “bedside manner”. De meesten van ons zoeken iemand die vertrouwen uitstraalt en lijkt te weten wat hij doet.

Vertrouwen staat niet gelijk aan bekwaamheid, en er zijn veel dokters (en mensen in andere vakgebieden) die een hoog zelfvertrouwen hebben, maar niet echt bekwaam zijn om de situatie aan te pakken.

Hier kan wat onderzoek helpen. Ten eerste heeft uw dokter online beoordelingen, en die beoordelingen geven iets aan over het niveau van zorg dat zij patiënten bieden. Ten tweede, als wat uw zorgverlener u vertelt echt vreemd lijkt, is het gemakkelijk om wat onderzoek te doen naar de aandoening waarmee u naar verluidt te maken heeft en te zien of de symptomen kloppen en of de behandeling redelijk lijkt.

Het is belangrijk te beseffen dat mensen niet hetzelfde zijn als voertuigen. Hiermee bedoel ik dat er geen scantool bestaat die zorgverleners kunnen aansluiten om alle foutcodes te genereren en dan de dingen te repareren die die codes veroorzaken.

Zelfs als zorgverleners zeker zijn van de diagnose, reageren sommige patiënten niet op de eerste of zelfs de tweede beschikbare behandeling. Dat betekent niet dat de diagnose of de behandeling fout was, maar dat mensen geen klonen van elkaar zijn en sommigen beter reageren op het ene type behandeling dan op het andere.

Misschien zullen we op een dag genetische tests hebben die ons meteen vertellen wat het perfecte medicijn of behandelplan is voor een bepaalde ziekte, maar die dag lijkt nog ver weg.

Een laatste punt om te noemen is dat goede dokters zich niet bedreigd zullen voelen als hun patiënten vragen stellen of onderzoek doen. Er zijn tijden dat een patiënt mij vraagt naar een nieuwe behandeling waar ik niet mee bekend ben, en ik dan mijn eigen onderzoek moet doen.

Die situaties zijn voor mij geen ergernis maar een leermogelijkheid. “Daar ben ik niet mee bekend,” zeg ik tegen mijn patiënt. “Laat me wat onderzoek doen en met enkele specialisten die ik vertrouw spreken, dan bel ik u later deze week en laat ik u weten wat ik heb gevonden.”

Soms onderzoek ik en ontdek ik dat de behandeling duur is en weinig of gemengde voordelen lijkt te bieden, maar soms is het een verbetering ten opzichte van de vroegere methoden. Dokters moeten leren en hun manier van geneeskunde bedrijven aanpassen naarmate we nieuwe dingen leren over ziekten en hoe het menselijk lichaam erop reageert.

Nederigheid is nodig

Hoe langer ik geneeskunde beoefen, hoe minder ik het gevoel heb dat ik weet. Het is niet dat ik dementie ontwikkel, maar eerder dat ik besef dat er talrijke ziekten zijn waarvoor we geen goede behandelingen hebben. Het menselijk lichaam is verbazingwekkend complex. Er zijn 36 biljoen cellen in het menselijk lichaam, en normaal werken ze allemaal perfect samen; het probleem is uit te vinden wat te doen als dat niet gebeurt.

Het Dunning-Kruger-effect is iets dat veel vakgebieden beïnvloedt waarbij mensen met beperkte kennis en vaardigheid hun capaciteiten in dat vakveld significant overschatten. Studies hebben aangetoond dat 65 procent van de Amerikanen gelooft dat ze een bovengemiddelde intelligentie hebben.4 Statistisch gezien is dat niet mogelijk. Vijftig procent van een willekeurige groep mensen zal boven gemiddeld zijn, en de andere 50 procent zal onder gemiddeld zijn. Zo is de IQ-schaal opgezet.

Hoewel dit effect aanwezig is bij dokters, geldt het ook voor patiënten. “Je onderzoek doen” is niet hetzelfde als vier jaar medische school voltooien, nog eens drie jaar in een opleidingsprogramma (residency) doorlopen en doorgaan met het bijhouden van ontwikkelingen in de geneeskunde via diverse nascholingscursussen. We zouden er allemaal goed aan doen beter te luisteren en onze beperkingen te erkennen.

Het feit dat de neef van uw moeder melkdistel-extract nam en zich veel beter voelde bij vergelijkbare klachten als die van u is interessant. Of het melkdistel-extract hen daadwerkelijk hielp van hun ziekte te herstellen, of er sprake was van een placebo-effect, of dat ze toch beter zouden zijn geworden ongeacht wat ze namen, staat ter discussie.

Ware wijsheid

Ik heb al over wijsheid gesproken, en daarmee wil ik afsluiten. Ware wijsheid is beseffen dat genezing van God komt. Psalm 103:3 zegt over God: “Die al uw krankheden geneest.”

Genezing komt niet van antibiotica of chemotherapie. Het komt niet van het nemen van de juiste supplementen of zelfs van het eten van een gezond dieet. Genezing komt omdat God ons aanraakt, tot in de kleinste deeltjes van onze cellen en ons immuunsysteem, en dingen weer heel maakt.

Ik geloof dat Hij soms door de geneeskunde heen werkt, maar andere keren door het effectieve, vurige gebed van rechtvaardige mannen en vrouwen. (Jakobus 5:16)

Met al onze kennis is het gemakkelijk om opgeblazen te raken van trots en te geloven dat we niemand anders nodig hebben. We leven in een wereld die wemelt van kennis en een wereld waarin wijsheid naar de achtergrond is verwezen.

We moeten de bron van onze informatie zorgvuldig kiezen en beseffen dat we niet alles weten. Misschien is de reden waarom de vreze des Heren het begin der wijsheid is dat het de eerste stap is om onze trots terzijde te leggen en te beseffen dat wij een klein onderdeel van de schepping zijn. Alleen dan kunnen we nederig luisteren en leren en genezing ontvangen.

The people we commonly refer to as the Russian Mennonites came into being as a group in a way quite similar to that of us with an Anabaptist heritage. We sprang from the same areas of Europe, from much of the same teachings of early Anabaptism, and have both experienced many of the same temptations and pitfalls, though at different times and locations.

This article will not focus on the beginnings of the Russian Mennonites apart from a brief overview. The group first entered Russia upon the urgings of the Viceroy Potemkin, who came into authority over the area now known as Ukraine after its annexation by Russia in 1783. The area had been under his partial administration since 1774, and he was eager to populate the land with foreign settlers. The residents of New Russia, as it was then called, were mostly nomads and Cossacks, a seminomadic group present in the steppes of Russia. The Mennonites in Danzig, Poland, were first approached with the offer of land, which would have appealed to them because they were routinely denied land ownership as a semi-persecuted people at that time. This offer came in August of 1786, and two brothers from the Danzig church were sent to survey the land and make arrangements for possible immigration.

The first immigration of 462 families began in 1788, and the “Old Colony” was established at Chortitza. They were afforded freedom of religion, exemption from military service, and the right to maintain their own schools and governances.

The Mennonites thrived in their new homeland. Although the first years were hard, partially due to the fact that mostly poorer families and those not in church leadership chose to resettle in Russia, the group soon began to transform the barren plains and steppes into rich agricultural communities. As the churches grew, so did their prosperity.

This period of relative peace lasted for over a century, until the late 1800s, when the Russian government, dissatisfied with the number of foreign settlements inside its borders, began applying pressure to many of the groups it had invited to settle its land some 100 years before. The Mennonites were not the only ones targeted, as many groups from various nations had established themselves in Russia. Steps taken against the Mennonites included pressure to participate in the armed forces as well as pressure to drop the German language that the communities had been using in favor of the Russian language. As these pressures increased, some Mennonites chose to flee the country in the 1870s. The majority, however, by now quite wealthy and affluent in comparison to their Russian peasant neighbors, chose to stay and weather the storm.

Unbeknownst to them, a full-scale revolution that would reshape Russia as a country was just around the corner. In 1917, the Bolsheviks came to power through the October Revolution, an event where the reigning tsar, or emperor, was deposed and exiled, and a new government was set up. A civil war broke out, and much of the fighting raged over the lands occupied by the Mennonites. Here, it is necessary to insert a brief history of the ideology of this new government.

The October Revolution and its subsequent change in government were fueled by a class war. As opposed to Nazi Germany, where a person could be arrested and killed for their race, in Russia, a person could and would be arrested for their class, for example, property ownership was seen as a crime against the people, and so the wealthier class of Russian peasants and farmers, those who most often owned property and employed the lower class of peasants, became an instant target a revolution that claimed to want to distribute all property and resources evenly amongst its citizenry.

By this time, the strong agricultural society of the Mennonites had transformed Ukraine into a breadbasket, its vast fields sown with wheat developed specifically by the Mennonites: Turkey Red Wheat. This hardy crop had made the Mennonite church quite wealthy, and their colonies had grown and flourished into villages of comfort and, at times, extravagance. This must have been a two-fold insult to the still impoverished peasants of Russia. Not only was there a large group of people in their midst that taught, spoke, and did their dealings in a language not of the Motherland, but these people also were wealthy beyond most peasants’ dreams.

It is, therefore, no surprise that when the kulaks, the wealthy class of peasants, came under persecution from the new government, the Mennonites were seen as the enemy of the people. As the civil war raged over Mennonite lands, villages were burnt and decimated, people executed or driven off, and livestock and grain plundered. Eventually, this period of fighting did come to an end, but for those few who survived the destruction, there was no reprieve to be found.

With the label of kulak and being generally defenseless, the Mennonites faced intense persecution. Religious services were rarely allowed, and the agricultural communities that had fed Russia and many others besides were collectivized and put under government control. Many of their churches ceased to exist entirely, although those in the east tended to last longer than the western villages.

Imagine then, to a people accustomed for generations to the favor and benevolence of material possessions and success, that all things material are stripped away. In a historical eye blink, the wealthy become the poor, and the favored become the hated. Even with a strong Christian faith, such a turn of events would shock and confuse.

But further tests were yet ahead for those who endured the first 25 years of the Soviet persecution. With the memory of their easy lives still fresh, the dawn of World War II brought a unique and enticing opportunity: the rise of a government that promoted the well-being of the German race, that valued those groups that could turn an empty prairie into a sprawling farm, that was vehemently anti-Communist- to this beleaguered group of believers, this must have seemed to be a God sent miracle to deliver them from their burdensome exile.

And so, they embraced the invading Germans. We readers, who are blessed with the ability to see the end result of these people’s decisions, can certainly make a good guess at what the end result was of wholesale support for the Nazis, but we must remember the scenarios that these Mennonites found themselves in...it was not one that would have been easy to decipher and decide upon if it were to be judged by man’s knowledge.

And so it was that the descendants of those helpless believers who gave their bodies at the stake and sword aligned themselves with a worldly kingdom that promised to protect and provide for them. In exchange for an eternal heritage, they chose to hope that the might of the German army would win back their earthly heritage and riches, and it was in this might that they trusted, forming bands of men who fought alongside the Germans against their old neighbors.

History did not deviate from its course, and the German army was eventually beaten back to its own borders and then further, and yet further into German lands. Before this retreating army ran those that had looked to it for their deliverance.

The atrocities of the Soviet government against its citizens are well documented in various works, most famously in the Gulag Archipelago, a book written by a Russian officer who was accused of treason. That author, Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn, painted a terrible picture of the treatment and exile of those who had opposed the USSR. Amongst the imprisoned or executed millions described in his tomes, there lie the remnants of a people who began as we did, experienced the smile of prosperity as we do, and then, treasuring that prosperity, lost it in calamitous fashion. We would do well to consider the paths we choose, as the wise king of the Scriptures instructs us, lest we, too, fall in the pursuit of prosperity. “Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established” (Proverbs 4:26).

Watu tunaowaambia kwa kawaida Mennonites wa Kirusi walikuwepo kama kikundi kwa njia iliyo sawa sana na sisi wenye urithi wa Anabaptist. Tulitoka katika maeneo yale yale ya Ulaya, tukaibuka kutoka mafundisho mengi yale yale ya Anabaptism ya mwanzo, na sote tumepitia vishawishi na mitego mingi ile ile, ingawa kwa nyakati na katika maeneo tofauti.

Makala hii haitazingatia mwanzo wa Mennonites wa Kirusi isipokuwa muhtasari mfupi. Kikundi hicho kilianza kuingia Urusi kwa shinikizo la Vicero Potemkin, aliyepata mamlaka juu ya eneo linalojulikana sasa kama Ukraine baada ya kuunganishwa kwake na Urusi mwaka 1783. Eneo hilo lilikuwa chini ya utawala wake kwa sehemu tangu 1774, na alikuwa na hamu ya kuwakaa wakulima wa kigeni katika ardhi hiyo. Wakazi wa New Russia, kama ilivyokuwa ikitajwa wakati huo, waliokuwa zaidi wavamizi wa maeneo na Cossacks, kundi la nusu-wahamaji lililokuwa katika tambarare za Urusi. Mennonites waliokuwa Danzig, Poland, walipewa ofa ya ardhi kwa mara ya kwanza, ofa ambayo iliwaivutia kwa sababu kwa wakati huo walikuwa mara kwa mara wakikataliwa kumiliki ardhi kama watu walioteswa kwa kiasi. Ofa hii ilikuja Agosti 1786, na ndugu wawili kutoka kanisa la Danzig waliotumwa kukagua ardhi na kupanga uhamisho unaowezekana.

Uhamisho wa kwanza wa familia 462 ulianza mwaka 1788, na “Colony ya Kale” iliundwa Chortitza. Walipatiwa uhuru wa dini, msamaha wa utumishi wa kijeshi, na haki ya kudumisha shule zao na uongozi wao wenyewe.

Mennonites walistawi katika nchi yao mpya. Ingawa miaka ya mwanzo yalikuwa ngumu, kwa sehemu kwa sababu familia maskini zaidi na wale wasiotawala kanisani ndio walichagua kuhamia Urusi, kikundi hicho hivi karibuni kilianza kubadilisha tambarare za utupu na steppes kuwa jamii tajiri za kilimo. Kadiri makanisa yalivyokua, ndivyo pia ustawi wao ulivyoongezeka.

Kipindi hiki cha amani kwa kiasi kilidumu kwa zaidi ya karne, hadi mwishoni mwa miaka ya 1800, wakati serikali ya Kirusi, isiyoridhishwa na idadi ya makazi ya kigeni ndani ya mipaka yake, ilianza kubana vikundi vingi ilivyokuwa yaalikwa kuja kuabiri ardhi yake karibu miaka 100 kabla. Mennonites hawakuwa pekee waliondaliwa; vikundi vingi kutoka mataifa mbalimbali viliweka misingi yao Urusi. Hatua zilizochukuliwa dhidi ya Mennonites zilijumuisha shinikizo la kushiriki katika jeshi pamoja na shinikizo la kuacha lugha ya Kijerumani ambayo jamii zilikuwa zikitumia na badala yake kuchagua lugha ya Kirusi. Kadri vishinikizo hivi vilivyozidi, baadhi ya Mennonites waliamua kukimbia nchi hiyo miaka ya 1870. Hata hivyo wengi, ambao kwa sasa walikuwa matajiri na walikuwa na ustawi ikilinganishwa na majirani zao wakulima wa Kirusi, waliamua kubaki na kuvumilia dhoruba.

Wakijua au wasijui, mapinduzi ya kikamili yaliyorushia mabadiliko ya Urusi kama taifa yalikuwa karibu. Mwaka 1917, Wabolshiviki walichukua mamlaka kupitia Mapinduzi ya Oktoba, tukio ambapo tsar aliyekuwa akitawala, au mfalme, aliondolewa madarakani na kutawanywa, na serikali mpya ikaanzishwa. Vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe vilivuka, na mapigano mengi yalitokea juu ya ardhi zilizokuwa za Mennonites. Hapa, ni muhimu kuingiza historia fupi ya itikadi ya serikali hii mpya.

Mapinduzi ya Oktoba na mabadiliko ya serikali yaliyofuata yalichochewa na vita vya tabaka. Tofauti na Nazi Ujerumani, ambapo mtu angeweza kukamatwa na kuuliwa kwa sababu ya ukoo wake, huko Urusi, mtu angekamatwa kwa tabaka lake; kwa mfano, umiliki wa mali ulionekana kama uhalifu dhidi ya watu, na hivyo tabaka la matajiri wa wakulima na wakulima wa Kirusha, wale waliokuwa mara nyingi wanamiliki mali na kuajiri wakulima wa tabaka la chini, likawa lengo la mapinduzi ambayo ilidai kutaka kugawa mali na rasilimali sawia kwa raia zake.

Wakati huo, jamii imara ya kilimo ya Mennonites ilikuwa imegeuza Ukraine kuwa mfuko wa ngano, mashamba yake makubwa yakiwa yameibwa ngano iliyotengenezwa mahsusi na Mennonites: Ngano ya Turkey Red. Mazao haya yenye nguvu yalifanya kanisa la Mennonite kuwa tajiri sana, na koloni zao zilikuwa zimeongezeka na kustawi kuwa vijiji vya starehe na, wakati mwingine, unyenyekevu wa kupindukia. Hili lilikuwa ni kashfa kwa mara mbili kwa wakulima waliokuwa bado maskini wa Urusi. Si tu kulikuwa kundi kubwa la watu katikati yao waliofundisha, walizungumza, na kufanya miamala yao kwa lugha isiyo ya Nchi yao, bali watu hawa pia walikuwa matajiri kuliko ndoto za wakulima wengi.

Kwa hivyo, si ajabu kwamba wakati kulak, tabaka la wakulima matajiri, likitendewa kwa ukatili na serikali mpya, Mennonites walionekana kama adui wa watu. Wakati vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe vilipogonga kwenye ardhi za Mennonite, vijiji vilichomwa moto na kulaharibiwa, watu waliuawa au wakatupwa mbali, na wanyama wa kufugwa na nafaka zikachukuliwa. Hatimaye, kipindi hiki cha mapigano kilikuja kikamalie, lakini kwa wale wachache waliobaki baada ya uharibifu, hakukuwa na mapumziko ya kupatikana.

Kwa lebo ya kulak na kuto uwezo wa kujitetea, Mennonites walikumbana na mateso makali. Ibada za kidini mara chache ziliruhusiwa, na jamii za kilimo zilizokuwa zikiliwahi kula Urusi na wengine wengi zilikusanywa kanuni za umiliki wa pamoja (collectivized) na kuwekwa chini ya udhibiti wa serikali. Makanisa mengi yalisimama kutokuwepo kabisa, ingawa yale mashariki yalidumu kwa muda mrefu kuliko vijiji vya magharibi.

Fikiria basi, kwa watu waliokuwa wamezoea vizazi kwa vizazi upendeleo na fadhila za umiliki wa mali na mafanikio, kwamba vitu vyote vya kimwili vimeondolewa. Kwa kiganjo cha kihistoria, matajiri wakawa masikini, na waliopewa walivyokuwa chukiwa. Hata akiwa na imani thabiti ya Kikristo, mabadiliko kama hayo yangeshtua na kuchanganya.

Lakini majaribu zaidi yalikuwa mbele kwa wale waliovumilia miaka ya kwanza 25 ya mateso ya Soviet. Ukiwa bado na kumbukumbu ya maisha yao ya urahisi, alfajiri ya Vita Kuu ya Pili vya Dunia ilileta fursa ya kipekee na ya kuvutia: kuibuka kwa serikali iliyokuza ustawi wa ukoo wa Kijerumani, iliyothamini vikundi vilivyoweza kugeuza tambarare tupu kuwa shamba kubwa, na ambayo ilikuwa kwa msimamo mkali dhidi ya Kialamu (Anti-Communist) — kwa kundi hili la waumini walioteseka, hili lilionekana kama muujiza uliotumwa na Mungu kuwatoa kwenye uchomoro wao wa kifungo.

Na hivyo, walikumbatia Wajerumani waliotovuliwa. Sisi wasomaji, walio na baraka ya uwezo wa kuona matokeo ya mwisho ya maamuzi ya watu hawa, tunaweza hakika kukisia kwa busara matokeo ya maungwa mkono kwa wingi kwa Nazi, lakini tunapaswa kukumbuka hali ambazo Mennonites hawa walikuwa wamejipata ndani yake... haikuwa hali ambayo ingekuwa rahisi kutafsiri na kuamua ikiwa ingepewa hukumu kwa maarifa ya mwanadamu.

Na hivyo ilivyokuwa kwamba mabaki ya waumini wasio na msaada waliokuwa waliweka miili yao katika mwiba na upanga walijiweka upande wa ufalme wa kidunia uliowaahidi kuwalinda na kuwapa. Badala ya urithi wa milele, waliamua kutegemea kwamba nguvu za jeshi la Kijerumani zitanirejesha urithi wao wa kidunia na utajiri, na ndiyo katika nguvu hizi walitamani, wakitengeneza makundi ya wanaume waliopigana pamoja na Wajerumani dhidi ya majirani zao wa zamani.

Historia haikugeuka, na jeshi la Kijerumani hatimaye likashindwa kurudishwa hadi mipaka yake mwenyewe na kisha zaidi, na zaidi ndani ya maeneo ya Kijerumani. Kabla ya jeshi hili lilipojirejesha, walitoroka wale waliotegemea kwa wokovu wao.

Ukatili wa serikali ya Soviet dhidi ya raia wake umeandikwa vyema katika vitabu mbalimbali, maarufu zaidi katika Gulag Archipelago, kitabu kilichoandikwa na afisa wa Kirusi aliyedaiwa kuwa mwasi. Mwandishi huyo, Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn, alichora picha mbaya ya matibabu na kutawanywa kwa wale waliokataa USSR. Miongoni mwa waliofungwa au kuuawa mamilioni kama alivyoyaelezea katika vitabu vyake, kunabaki mabaki ya watu ambao walianza kama sisi, wakafurahia tabasamu la ustawi kama sisi, na kisha, wakiyathamini ustawi huo, wakaupoteza kwa njia ya maafa. A Christ-centered Courtship is a series of messages on godly courtship preached by Paul Hershberger. He preached these messages several times at different locations over the last ten years. Recently, we had them transcribed and abridged for reading clarity. After printing all five articles in The Heartbeat of the Remnant, we will publish them in a booklet. This is the fourth article of five.

There are five goals for this series:

  1. To turn the hearts of the fathers to their children.
  2. To turn the hearts of the children to their fathers.
  3. That parents would get a burden to lead their children into the perfect will of God for their lives.
  4. That young people would get a burden to seek God, find fulfillment and purpose in walking with God, and mature in their manners and character.
  5. That young men and women would rise up to be godly fathers and mothers with a vision to raise another godly generation.

We discussed Satan’s Snares for male and female in the last issue. Today’s topic is about waiting on God’s timing and plan for marriage.

The Preparation Sleep.

In Genesis 2:21, we read that Adam slept a deep sleep. God did surgery on him, and there was no anesthesiologist there to help with the surgery. Adam just slept a deep sleep.

We’re not talking about a dormant sleep, where we are unaware of our surroundings, but rather a germinating sleep. Germination has two components. The first component is dying and losing our identity. The second component is springing forth a new life. Preparation sleep is a sleep that is willing to die to self and lose its identity and its agenda. And yet, through this dying process, a new life can spring forth. Christians have the blessed opportunity to die to ourselves so that we can have fresh germination coming out of our lives. When we die to ourselves, new life springs forth.

“And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof. And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him. And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man” (Genesis 2:19–22).

In Genesis 2:20, Adam became aware that there was no helper suitable for him. As all the animals went by, he began to realize his need. Each animal had a male and a female, but he was the only one like him. God’s advice for Adam was, “You need to go to sleep.” And as Adam slept that deep sleep, he was wholly yielded. As Adam slept, God prepared for him a helpmeet. Adam did not interfere with this process. He wasn’t giving advice: “Make her this way or that way. ” This was all God’s doing, and Adam was yielded and in a deep sleep with no plan of his own. Today, this also applies to Eve. In Adam’s day, Eve wasn’t created yet. Today, Eve is alive the same as Adam is. In other words, today, we have males and females. If Eve doesn’t go into this preparation sleep as well, Adam will have difficulty going into a preparation sleep if Eve tries to get his attention. Eve needs to go to sleep in the same way as Adam does.

Young men and women, it is important that you yield your future and marriage to God. If you try to take your future into your own hands, you will likely fail. God has a purpose and plan for each one of you. It is possible that God’s plan for you is not marriage. But God does have a plan for you.

As we consider preparation sleep, let’s look at the life of Jesus when He was young. We want to look at four points from His life and make practical applications.

Jesus was a maturing, godly young man

“And when they had performed all things according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth. This was right after they had been at the temple. And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon him. Now, his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the Passover. And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem after the custom of the feast” (Luke 2:39–42).

In this scripture, Jesus is twelve years old. If you are twelve years old or older, I urge you to sit up and take note. Jesus was twelve, and here’s what it says about Him: “And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon Him.” What an example of a maturing, godly young man. He “waxed strong in spirit.” That means the power of the Holy Ghost was strong upon Him. He was “filled with wisdom”—the wisdom of God! “And the grace of God”—the divine influence from God that helps one live a godly life, was upon Him, too.

Jesus began preparing for His life ministry at a young age. Sometimes, we think childhood is a time for playing. I’m not against children playing, but youth must consider what life is about long before adulthood. If you plan to wait until the time for marriage to get serious, you’ve missed a tremendous opportunity. Prepare yourself for marriage so you are ready to be married when that day comes. Then God’s face will shine upon you and bless you, and your life will be fulfilled and fruitful. There’s a preparation that goes on during this sleep.

Jesus sensed the call of God

“And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem after the custom of the feast. And when they had fulfilled the days, as they returned, the child Jesus tarried behind in Jerusalem; and Joseph and his mother knew not of it. But they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day’s journey; and they sought him among their kinsfolk and acquaintance. And when they found him not, they turned back again to Jerusalem, seeking him. And it came to pass, that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions. And all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers. And when they saw him, they were amazed: and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing. And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business? And they understood not the saying which he spake unto them” (Luke 2:42-50).

At twelve years old, Jesus was already deeply interested in the Word of God. The calling of God was very clear to Him. When his parents came looking for him, he said, “Why did you look for me? Don’t you know that I need to be about My Father’s business?”

Young men and women, do you sense the calling of God? Is the Spirit of God speaking into your lives, moving, and giving direction? If we live a shallow Christian life, we won’t sense the moving of the Spirit of God. But if we get close to God, the Bible says He’ll draw nigh to us.

Do you understand the Bible, and can you give answers to what you believe? It is important to lay your own foundation. You can’t build on Mom and Dad’s foundation. If you grew up in a godly Christian home, you are blessed. But don’t be lazy; develop your own convictions. Find out for yourself what the Word of God says. Talk to Dad or Mom if you don’t understand something. Lay a foundation so you are ready to be married when the day comes.

Jesus was subject to his parents

“And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them: but his mother kept all these sayings in her heart” (Luke 2:51).

The example of Jesus is clear: “I must be about My Father’s business.” But He laid down His will and waited. He went home with his parents and “was subject to them.” He waited for eighteen years. Jesus continued actively pursuing His relationship with His Father in heaven in those eighteen years. He prepared for His ministry while He waited.

Sometimes, we wonder why we have to wait. We can’t see any purpose, and it feels like we’re being held back. But God works in our hearts while we wait and prepare for what’s ahead.

Jesus continued to increase and mature

“And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man” (Luke 2:52). Waiting and “preparation” sleeping didn’t hold Jesus back. As we consider His ministry and all the difficult things He faced, we know he prepared. How could He have such wisdom to have the correct answer to every question or give the right response? He prepared, and He walked with God.

Learning to walk with God

We, too, want to grow in wisdom, stature, and favor with God. To do so, we must learn to walk with God. We learn to walk with God by:

Bible reading

2 Timothy 2:15 says, “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” Constructive daily Bible reading is like constructing a building. It takes time. In the same way, we can’t become a Bible scholar in one year. We don’t read our Bibles just to survive for the day. If we’re reading to survive today, we are not laying bricks in our spiritual building. We need to lay some bricks. If we lay a few bricks every day, after some years, there will be quite a structure if we do it with a plan. Constructive daily Bible reading doesn’t need to be huge but should add up.

Prayer

“I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth” (1 Timothy 2:1–4).

Pray and intercede for other people. Thank God for what He has done for you. If God answered specific prayer requests, thank Him for it. Pray about specific needs in your life. “Lord, what are areas of need in my life? Take one or two of these areas, and seek God for grace to overcome them. If you do this for several years, God will abundantly bless your preparation.

Take time to praise and thank God. “By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name” (Hebrews 13:15). Thankfulness coming out of our hearts and lives is important. God inhabits the praises of His people. When we are downcast, one of the best things we can do is sing. Rejoice in the Lord; bless His name.

Learn to hear the voice of God

Learn to discern God’s will and leading. Young people often struggle in this area. But as we learn to walk with God, we keep growing one step at a time. We read our Bibles, study, meditate, and memorize verses. We pray, fast, and seek the Lord. We praise Him and give Him thanks. We intercede for others and ask Him to help us. As we do these spiritual exercises, we begin to know the voice of God. He’ll begin to lead us in ways that we can understand. But we must take a step at a time and keep going. Don’t just aim at survival. Prepare for life.

Die to areas in your life

You need to die to your flesh so you can have that germination come forth into newness of life. Our flesh shrinks back from the idea of dying and says, “That’s not pleasant. I don’t enjoy that.” Our flesh doesn’t enjoy it, but dying to self brings forth new life. We can experience a springing forth in a new life as much as we are willing to die to ourselves.

Developing a Christlike character

Developing a Christlike character can be one of those areas in our lives where we struggle the hardest. But let’s not shrink away from it. We have the grace of God on our side, and he wants to give us inner strength so we can overcome areas of need in our lives.

Consider the fruits of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22–23. This is a good place to start developing a Christlike character. Love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, and temperance. I still go back and look at that list, asking, “Ok, how am I doing?” If I claim to have the Spirit of God living in my heart, I should have these things coming out of my life. Let’s keep pressing on into the Kingdom.

When developing a Christlike character, let’s ask: What spirit comes from me? Do I have a loud spirit or a quiet spirit? A harsh spirit or a gentle spirit? A critical spirit or a forgiving spirit? A proud spirit or a humble spirit? A selfish spirit or a servant spirit? Unkind or kind? Crude or mannerly? Tough or compassionate? Rude or respectful? Do I need to work on my character?

Yield your life to God’s service

Art thou bound unto a wife? seek not to be loosed. Art thou loosed from a wife? seek not a wife. But and if thou marry, thou hast not sinned; and if a virgin marry, she hath not sinned. Nevertheless such shall have trouble in the flesh: but I spare you. But I would have you without carefulness. He that is unmarried careth for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please the Lord. But he that is married careth for the things that are of the world, how he may please his wife. There is difference also between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman careth for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit: but she that is married careth for the things of the world, how she may please her husband” (1 Cor. 7:2–28, 32–34).

If you are unmarried, it may feel like “God has no purpose for me.” God has a purpose for everyone. In fact, if young people cannot be content and fulfilled in serving the Lord as a single person, they are not ready for married life either. Contentment is caring about the things of the Lord.

It goes with this preparation sleep. If your mind is focused on, “I’ve got to get married!” or “I wonder whom I’ll get married to,” you will be distracted and won’t be able to prepare for God’s plan for your life. These areas in your life need to go to sleep. In God’s timing, He’ll cause it to spring forth in newness of life.

Find fulfillment in serving the Lord, walking with Him, and being content. Find contentment in serving others by starting at home. Also, find contentment and fulfillment in the church.

What kind of partner do I need?

This may seem like a different topic, but this, too, is a part of preparation. Ask yourself: “What kind of partner do I need?” When considering a partner, you need:

  1. One with a vision.
  2. One that is virtuous.
  3. One that has a godly character.
  4. One that is under authority.
  5. One who is in love with Jesus.

This is fairly broad and yet all-encompassing. This is the kind of partner you want.

Parents, talk to your children. Don’t wait till there’s a request from a young man. Or perhaps your son says, “Well, Dad, uh, I really sort of feel drawn to this girl.” Fathers, don’t wait, but prepare for it. Talk about it with your children. And yes, you may ask them to wait. You may want to help them go to sleep. Give them direction on it. This conversation needs to happen when they are a bit older. Maybe around 20 or 21, this conversation could begin.

Parents, pray about this matter. Sometimes, we clearly sense God’s direction for our child in marriage. Other times, we may not be sure and need to ask God for direction. Pray for your children before they seek marriage. We’re not looking for them to just “fall in love” one day.

When am I ready for marriage?

Here are some questions to consider:

  1. Am I mature? Have I learned to walk with God? Am I steady and stable and established in the faith? Or do I have major ups and downs?
  2. Do I have a godly character? How do I treat others? How do I treat my parents and my siblings? How do I treat my coworkers? Am I quiet, gentle, forgiving, humble, a servant, kind, mannerly, compassionate, and respectful?
  3. Am I under authority? This one is important. Have you dealt with your strong nature? Are you willing to be compatible, like Ephesians 5:21 says about “submitting one to another”? Have you learned to honor and respect your father? Are you under authority?
  4. Is Jesus my all in all? Am I married to Christ? Do I find satisfaction in Him?
  5. Am I content with my lot in life? Am I willing to live with less than Mom and Dad have? You cannot start in the same place in life where your parents are today. Do I desire material things, always reaching for more?

Young men

Study Titus 2:6-8

  1. Young men, can you spiritually lead a wife and children? Can you do what Ephesians 5:24-27 says about washing them with the Word and guiding a home spiritually?
  2. Are you able to financially provide? Can you take care of the household? When you marry, it’s not just yourself but your wife and children to provide for.
  3. Are you an overcomer in moral purity? Are you walking in victory?
  4. Are you disciplined to say no to yourself? Are you willing to sacrifice for the good of others? Marriage brings sacrifice. Can you surrender to others?
  5. Are you willing to give up your independence? Are you ready for marriage? Marriage is about two people, not just yourself.

Young women

Study Titus 2:4–5.

  1. Do you have a meek and quiet spirit? A spirit that is restful and content?
  2. Are you able to become someone’s helpmeet? Can you be the rib at his side?
  3. Are you willing to take on his identity, goals, and visions? Are you willing to do that?
  4. Do you enjoy being a keeper at home? Have you learned homemaking skills?
  5. Do you love children? Are your young siblings a bother to you? Will you love your children?

In Summary

In Luke 2:51 Jesus “went down with them [His parents] and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them: but his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.” Even though we can’t see the future, God will bless us when we submit ourselves. At the age of 12, Jesus clearly sensed that call of God. “I must be about my Father’s business.” But He submitted Himself and went home.

Now, it is eighteen years later. “Now when all the people were baptized, it came to pass, that Jesus also being baptized, and praying, the heaven was opened, And the Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove upon him, and a voice came from heaven, which said, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased. And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age . . . ” (Luke 3:21–23).

Jesus sensed that clear call from God at age 12. Yet He submitted Himself to His parents, who didn’t understand, and He prepared during the next 18 years. Now heaven opened, and God said, “Thou art My beloved Son, in whom I am well-pleased!” What more could we desire? Nothing else will matter if we get to heaven one day and hear those words.

Jesus prepared over eighteen years for His three years of ministry, but it was the most effective three years of ministry anybody ever has had and will ever have. He prepared!

God has a plan for each one of our lives. Can we yield to His leading and timing? Let’s germinate, dying to ourselves and springing forth into the newness of life. Let’s be in a germinating sleep. We may not understand it all, but let’s prepare, germinate, grow, and increase in the grace of God. My young brother and sister, just take one step at a time, and God will bless your life.

A Christ-centered Courtship è una serie di messaggi sul corteggiamento secondo Dio predicati da Paul Hershberger. Ha predicato questi messaggi più volte in diversi luoghi negli ultimi dieci anni. Recentemente li abbiamo trascritti e ridotti per chiarezza di lettura. Dopo aver stampato tutti e cinque gli articoli in The Heartbeat of the Remnant, li pubblicheremo in opuscolo. Questo è il quarto di cinque articoli.

Ci sono cinque obiettivi per questa serie:

  1. Rivolgere i cuori dei padri verso i loro figli.
  2. Rivolgere i cuori dei figli verso i loro padri.
  3. Che i genitori acquisiscano il peso di guidare i loro figli nella perfetta volontà di Dio per le loro vite.
  4. Che i giovani acquisiscano il peso di cercare Dio, trovare appagamento e scopo camminando con Dio, e maturare nei modi e nel carattere.
  5. Che i giovani uomini e donne si levino a essere padri e madri pii con la visione di crescere un’altra generazione pia.

Nel numero scorso abbiamo discusso le insidie di Satana per maschi e femmine. L’argomento di oggi riguarda l’attendere il tempo e il piano di Dio per il matrimonio.

The Preparation Sleep.

In Genesi 2:21 leggiamo che Adamo cadde in un sonno profondo. Dio gli fece un’operazione, e non c’era un anestesista lì ad aiutare con l’intervento. Adamo semplicemente dormì un sonno profondo.

Non stiamo parlando di un sonno dormiente, in cui non siamo consapevoli di ciò che ci circonda, ma piuttosto di un sonno germinante. La germinazione ha due componenti. La prima componente è morire e perdere la nostra identità. La seconda componente è germogliare una nuova vita. Il sonno di preparazione è un sonno disposto a morire a se stesso e a perdere la propria identità e il proprio programma. Eppure, attraverso questo processo di morire, può germogliare una nuova vita. I cristiani hanno la benedetta opportunità di morire a se stessi così da poter avere una fresca germinazione che esca dalle loro vite. Quando moriamo a noi stessi, la nuova vita germoglia.

“E dal suolo il Signore Dio formò ogni animale della campagna e ogni uccello del cielo; e li condusse ad Adamo perché vedesse come li avrebbe chiamati; e qualunque nome Adamo avesse dato a ogni essere vivente, quello fu il suo nome. E Adamo diede nomi a tutto il bestiame, agli uccelli del cielo e a ogni animale della campagna; ma per Adamo non si trovò un aiuto adatto a lui. Allora il Signore Dio fece cadere un profondo sonno su Adamo, e mentre questi dormiva, gli tolse una delle costole e richiuse la carne al suo posto; e dalla costola che il Signore Dio aveva tolto all'uomo, egli formò una donna e la condusse all'uomo” (Genesi 2:19–22).

In Genesi 2:20 Adamo si accorse che non c’era un aiuto adatto a lui. Mentre tutti gli animali passavano davanti a lui, cominciò a rendersi conto del suo bisogno. Ogni animale aveva un maschio e una femmina, ma lui era l’unico della sua specie. Il consiglio di Dio ad Adamo fu: “Devi andare a dormire.” E mentre Adamo dormiva quel sonno profondo, si era totalmente arreso. Mentre Adamo dormiva, Dio gli preparò un aiuto idoneo. Adamo non interferì in questo processo. Non dava consigli: “Falla così o cosà.” Tutto ciò era opera di Dio, ed Adamo era rassegnato e in un sonno profondo senza un piano proprio. Oggi, questo si applica anche ad Eva. Ai tempi di Adamo Eva non era ancora stata creata. Oggi Eva è viva nello stesso modo in cui lo è Adamo. In altre parole, oggi abbiamo maschi e femmine. Se anche Eva non entra in questo sonno di preparazione, Adamo farà fatica ad entrarvi se Eva cerca di attirare la sua attenzione. Eva deve andare a dormire nello stesso modo in cui lo fa Adamo.

Giovani uomini e donne, è importante che consegniate il vostro futuro e il vostro matrimonio a Dio. Se cercate di prendere il vostro futuro nelle vostre mani, probabilmente fallirete. Dio ha uno scopo e un piano per ciascuno di voi. È possibile che il piano di Dio per voi non sia il matrimonio. Ma Dio ha un piano per voi.

Allorchè consideriamo il sonno di preparazione, guardiamo alla vita di Gesù quando era giovane. Vogliamo prendere quattro punti dalla Sua vita e trarre applicazioni pratiche.

Jesus was a maturing, godly young man

“E quando ebbero compiuto ogni cosa secondo la legge del Signore, tornarono in Galilea, alla loro città di Nazaret. Questo fu subito dopo che erano stati nel tempio. Il fanciullo crebbe e si fortificò nello spirito, pieno di sapienza, e la grazia di Dio era su di lui. I suoi genitori andavano ogni anno a Gerusalemme alla festa della Pasqua; e quand'egli aveva dodici anni, salirono a Gerusalemme secondo l’usanza della festa” (Luca 2:39–42).

In questo passo Gesù ha dodici anni. Se hai dodici anni o più, ti esorto a metterti in ascolto e a prendere nota. Gesù aveva dodici anni, e ecco cosa si dice di Lui: “Il fanciullo crebbe e si fortificò nello spirito, pieno di sapienza, e la grazia di Dio era su di lui.” Che esempio di giovane che matura e timorato di Dio. Si “fortificò nello spirito.” Ciò significa che il potere dello Spirito Santo era forte su di Lui. Era “pieno di sapienza”—la sapienza di Dio! “E la grazia di Dio”—l’influsso divino da parte di Dio che aiuta a vivere una vita pia—era anche su di Lui.

Gesù cominciò a prepararsi per il Suo ministero di vita fin da giovane. A volte pensiamo che l’infanzia sia tempo solo per giocare. Non sono contrario a che i bambini giochino, ma i giovani devono considerare di cosa si tratta la vita molto prima dell’età adulta. Se prevedi di aspettare fino al tempo del matrimonio per diventare serio, hai perso una tremenda opportunità. Preparati per il matrimonio così sarai pronto quando quel giorno arriverà. Allora il volto di Dio ti sorriderà e ti benedirà, e la tua vita sarà appagata e fruttuosa. C’è una preparazione che avviene durante questo sonno.

Jesus sensed the call of God

“E quando ebbero adempiuto i giorni, nel tornare, il fanciullo Gesù rimase a Gerusalemme e Giuseppe e sua madre non se ne accorsero. Pensando che fosse nella comitiva, fecero un giorno di cammino e lo cercarono fra i parenti e i conoscenti; e non trovandolo, tornarono a Gerusalemme per cercarlo. Dopo tre giorni lo trovarono nel tempio, seduto in mezzo ai dottori, mentre li ascoltava e faceva loro domande; e tutti quelli che lo udivano si stupivano della sua intelligenza e delle sue risposte. E vedendolo, rimasero meravigliati; e sua madre gli disse: Figlio, perché ci hai fatto così? Ecco, tuo padre e io ti abbiamo cercato angosciati. Ed egli disse loro: Perché mi cercavate? Non sapevate che devo occuparmi delle cose del Padre mio? Ma essi non compresero il discorso che aveva loro fatto” (Luca 2:42-50).

A dodici anni Gesù era già profondamente interessato alla Parola di Dio. La chiamata di Dio era molto chiara per Lui. Quando i suoi genitori vennero a cercarlo, disse: “Perché mi cercavate? Non sapete che devo occuparmi delle cose del Padre mio?”

Giovani uomini e donne, percepite la chiamata di Dio? Lo Spirito di Dio sta parlando nelle vostre vite, si muove e dà direzione? Se viviamo una vita cristiana superficiale, non percepiremo il movimento dello Spirito di Dio. Ma se ci avviciniamo a Dio, la Bibbia dice che Egli si avvicinerà a noi.

Capite la Bibbia, e sapete dare risposte a ciò in cui credete? È importante porre le proprie fondamenta. Non potete costruire sulla sola fondazione di mamma e papà. Se siete cresciuti in una casa cristiana pia, siete benedetti. Ma non siate pigri; sviluppate le vostre convinzioni. Scoprite da voi stessi cosa dice la Parola di Dio. Parlate con papà o mamma se non capite qualcosa. Ponete una base così che sarete pronti a sposarvi quando arriverà il giorno.

Jesus was subject to his parents

“E discese con loro e venne a Nazaret e stava loro soggetto; ma sua madre conservava tutte queste cose meditandole nel suo cuore” (Luca 2:51).

L’esempio di Gesù è chiaro: “Devo occuparmi delle cose del Padre mio.” Ma depose la Sua volontà e aspettò. Tornò a casa con i suoi genitori e “stava loro soggetto.” Aspettò per diciotto anni. Gesù continuò a perseguire attivamente la Sua relazione con il Padre celeste in quegli diciotto anni. Si preparò per il Suo ministero mentre aspettava.

A volte ci chiediamo perché dobbiamo aspettare. Non riusciamo a vedere alcuno scopo, e sembra che ci si tratti da trattenere. Ma Dio opera nei nostri cuori mentre aspettiamo e ci prepariamo per ciò che verrà.

Jesus continued to increase and mature

“E Gesù cresceva in sapienza e in statura, e in grazia presso Dio e gli uomini” (Luca 2:52). L’attendere e il “sonno di preparazione” non trattennero Gesù. Considerando il Suo ministero e tutte le cose difficili che affrontò, sappiamo che si preparò. Come poteva avere tale sapienza per dare la risposta corretta a ogni domanda o dare la risposta giusta? Si preparò e camminò con Dio.

Learning to walk with God

Noi vogliamo anch’essi crescere in sapienza, statura e grazia presso Dio. Per farlo dobbiamo imparare a camminare con Dio. Impariamo a camminare con Dio mediante:

Bible reading

2 Timoteo 2:15 dice: “Studia ad adoperarti approvato davanti a Dio, operaio che non abbia di che vergognarsi, che divida rettamente la parola della verità.” La lettura costruttiva quotidiana della Bibbia è come costruire un edificio. Ci vuole tempo. Allo stesso modo, non si può diventare studiosi della Bibbia in un anno. Non leggiamo le nostre Bibbie solo per sopravvivere al giorno. Se leggiamo per sopravvivere oggi, non stiamo posando mattoni nel nostro edificio spirituale. Dobbiamo posare alcuni mattoni. Se posiamo qualche mattone ogni giorno, dopo alcuni anni ci sarà una struttura se lo facciamo con un piano. La lettura quotidiana costruttiva della Bibbia non deve essere enorme, ma deve sommarsi.

Prayer

“Esorto dunque, prima di tutto, che si facciano suppliche, preghiere, intercessioni e rendimenti di grazie per tutti gli uomini; per i re e per tutti quelli che sono in autorità, affinché possiamo condurre una vita quieta e tranquilla in tutta pietà e dignità. Questo è buono e gradito al Salvatore nostro Dio, il quale vuole che tutti gli uomini siano salvati e vengano alla conoscenza della verità” (1 Timoteo 2:1–4).

Prega e intercedi per altre persone. Ringrazia Dio per ciò che ha fatto per te. Se Dio ha risposto a richieste di preghiera specifiche, ringrazialo per questo. Prega per bisogni specifici nella tua vita. “Signore, quali sono le aree di bisogno nella mia vita? Prendi una o due di queste aree e cerca Dio per grazia per superarle.” Se farai questo per diversi anni, Dio benedirà abbondantemente la tua preparazione.

Prenditi del tempo per lodare e ringraziare Dio. “Per lui dunque offriamo continuamente a Dio il sacrificio di lode, cioè il frutto di labbra che confessano il suo nome” (Ebrei 13:15). La gratitudine che esce dai nostri cuori e dalle nostre vite è importante. Dio abita le lodi del suo popolo. Quando siamo abbattuti, una delle cose migliori che possiamo fare è cantare. Rallegrati nel Signore; benedici il suo nome.

Learn to hear the voice of God

Impara a discernere la volontà e la guida di Dio. I giovani spesso faticano in quest’area. Ma mentre impariamo a camminare con Dio, continuiamo a crescere un passo alla volta. Leggiamo le nostre Bibbie, studiamo, meditiamo e memorizziamo versetti. Preghiamo, digiuni, e cerchiamo il Signore. Lo lodiamo e gli rendiamo grazie. Intercediamo per gli altri e gli chiediamo di aiutarci. Man mano che pratichiamo questi esercizi spirituali, cominciamo a conoscere la voce di Dio. Egli comincerà a guidarci in modi che possiamo comprendere. Ma dobbiamo prendere un passo alla volta e continuare. Non mirare solo alla sopravvivenza. Preparati per la vita.

Die to areas in your life

Devi morire alla tua carne affinché quella germinazione possa uscire in novità di vita. La nostra carne si ritrarrà dall’idea di morire e dirà: “Non è piacevole. Non mi piace.” La nostra carne non gode di ciò, ma morire a se stessi fa emergere nuova vita. Possiamo esperimentare un germogliare in una nuova vita nella misura in cui siamo disposti a morire a noi stessi.

Developing a Christlike character

La formazione di un carattere simile a Cristo può essere una di quelle aree delle nostre vite in cui lottiamo di più. Ma non dobbiamo sottrarci. Abbiamo la grazia di Dio dalla nostra parte, e Lui vuole darci forza interiore così possiamo superare le aree di bisogno nelle nostre vite.

Considera i frutti dello Spirito in Galati 5:22–23. Questo è un buon punto di partenza per sviluppare un carattere simile a Cristo. Amore, gioia, pace, longanimità, gentilezza, bontà, fede, mansuetudine e temperanza. Torno ancora a quella lista, chiedendo: “Ok, come vado?” Se affermo di avere lo Spirito di Dio che dimora nel mio cuore, dovrei avere queste cose che emergono dalla mia vita. Continuiamo a progredire nel Regno.

Quando sviluppiamo un carattere simile a Cristo, chiediamoci: quale spirito viene da me? Ho uno spirito forte o uno spirito tranquillo? Uno spirito aspro o uno spirito gentile? Uno spirito critico o uno spirito perdonante? Uno spirito orgoglioso o uno spirito umile? Uno spirito egoista o uno spirito di servizio? Scortese o cortese? Rozzo o garbato? Duro o compassionevole? Villano o rispettoso? Devo lavorare sul mio carattere?

Yield your life to God’s service

Se sei legato ad una moglie, non cerchi di essere sciolto. Se sei libero da una moglie, non cerchi una moglie. Ma se ti sposi, non peccasti; e se una vergine si marita, non peccò. Tuttavia avranno afflizione nella carne; io però vi risparmio. Vorrei infatti che foste senza preoccupazioni. Colui che è non sposato si cura delle cose del Signore, come piacere al Signore; ma colui che è sposato si cura delle cose del mondo, come piacere alla moglie. Anche la donna non sposata si cura delle cose del Signore, affinché sia santa nel corpo e nello spirito; ma quella sposata si cura delle cose del mondo, come piacere al marito” (1 Cor. 7:2–28, 32–34).

Se sei non sposato, può sembrarti che “Dio non abbia uno scopo per me.” Dio ha uno scopo per tutti. Anzi, se i giovani non possono essere contenti e appagati nel servire il Signore come singoli, non sono pronti nemmeno per la vita coniugale. La contentezza è preoccuparsi delle cose del Signore.

Questo va con il sonno di preparazione. Se la tua mente è focalizzata su: “Devo sposarmi!” o “Mi chiedo chi sposerò,” sarai distratto e non potrai prepararti per il piano di Dio per la tua vita. Queste aree della tua vita devono andare a dormire. Nel tempo di Dio, Egli farà sì che esse germoglino in novità di vita.

Trova appagamento nel servire il Signore, nel camminare con Lui e nell’essere contento. Trova contentezza nel servire gli altri iniziando in casa. Trova anche contentezza e appagamento nella chiesa.

What kind of partner do I need?

Questo può sembrare un argomento diverso, ma anche questo fa parte della preparazione. Chiediti: “Che tipo di partner mi serve?” Nel considerare un partner, hai bisogno di:

  1. Uno con una visione.
  2. Uno che sia virtuoso.
  3. Uno che abbia un carattere pia.
  4. Uno che sia sotto autorità.
  5. Uno che sia innamorato di Gesù.

Questo è abbastanza ampio e tuttavia comprensivo. Questo è il tipo di partner che desideri.

Genitori, parlate con i vostri figli. Non aspettate che ci sia una richiesta da un giovane. O forse vostro figlio dice: “Beh, papà, eh, mi sento un po’ attratto da questa ragazza.” Padri, non aspettate, ma preparatevi. Parlatene con i vostri figli. E sì, potete chiedere loro di aspettare. Potreste volerli aiutare ad andare a dormire. Date loro una direzione su questo. Questa conversazione deve avvenire quando sono un po’ più grandi. Forse intorno ai 20 o 21 anni, questa conversazione potrebbe cominciare.

Genitori, pregate su questa materia. A volte percepiamo chiaramente la direzione di Dio per nostro figlio nel matrimonio. Altre volte, potremmo non essere sicuri e dover chiedere a Dio la direzione. Pregate per i vostri figli prima che cerchino il matrimonio. Non vogliamo che semplicemente “si innamorino” un giorno.

When am I ready for marriage?

Ecco alcune domande da considerare:

  1. Sono maturo? Ho imparato a camminare con Dio? Sono saldo, stabile e stabilito nella fede? O ho grandi alti e bassi?
  2. Ho un carattere pia? Come tratto gli altri? Come tratto i miei genitori e i miei fratelli? Come tratto i miei colleghi di lavoro? Sono quieto, gentile, perdonante, umile, servizievole, gentile, garbato, compassionevole e rispettoso?
  3. Sono sotto autorità? Questo è importante. Hai affrontato la tua natura forte? Sei disposto ad essere compatibile, come dice Efesini 5:21 riguardo al “sottomettersi gli uni agli altri”? Hai imparato a onorare e rispettare tuo padre? Sei sotto autorità?
  4. Gesù è il mio tutto? Sono sposato con Cristo? Trovo soddisfazione in Lui?
  5. Sono contento della mia sorte nella vita? Sono disposto a vivere con meno di quanto hanno mamma e papà? Non puoi iniziare nella stessa posizione in cui sono i tuoi genitori oggi. Desidero le cose materiali, cercando sempre di più?

Young men

Study Titus 2:6-8

  1. Giovani uomini, potete guidare spiritualmente una moglie e dei figli? Potete fare ciò che Efesini 5:24-27 dice riguardo a lavarli con la Parola e guidare una casa spiritualmente?
  2. Siete in grado di provvedere finanziariamente? Potete provvedere per la casa? Quando vi sposate, non è solo voi stessi ma vostra moglie e i vostri figli da provvedere.
  3. Siete vincitori nella purezza morale? State camminando nella vittoria?
  4. Siete disciplinati a dire di no a voi stessi? Siete disposti a sacrificare per il bene degli altri? Il matrimonio porta sacrificio. Potete sottomettervi agli altri?
  5. Siete disposti a rinunciare alla vostra indipendenza? Siete pronti per il matrimonio? Il matrimonio riguarda due persone, non solo voi.

Young women

Study Titus 2:4–5.

  1. Hai uno spirito mite e quieto? Uno spirito riposante e contento?
  2. Sei in grado di diventare l’aiuto di qualcuno? Puoi essere la costola al suo fianco?
  3. Sei disposta a assumere la sua identità, i suoi obiettivi e le sue visioni? Sei disposta a farlo?
  4. Ti piace essere una custode della casa? Hai imparato abilità di gestione domestica?
  5. Ami i bambini? I tuoi fratellini ti danno fastidio? Amerai i tuoi figli?

In Summary

In Luca 2:51 Gesù “discese con loro [i suoi genitori] e venne a Nazaret, e stava loro soggetto; ma sua madre conservava tutte queste cose meditandole nel suo cuore.” Anche se non possiamo vedere il futuro, Dio ci benedirà quando ci sottomettiamo. All’età di 12 anni Gesù percepì chiaramente la chiamata di Dio. “Devo occuparmi delle cose del Padre mio.” Ma si sottomise e tornò a casa.

Ora sono passati diciotto anni. “Quando tutto il popolo fu battezzato, avvenne anche che Gesù, che era stato battezzato e che pregava, il cielo si aprì, e lo Spirito Santo discese corporativamente come una colomba su di lui, e una voce venne dal cielo, che disse: Tu sei il mio Figlio prediletto; in te mi sono compiaciuto. E Gesù stesso cominciò ad essere verso i trent'anni…” (Luca 3:21–23).

Gesù percepì quella chiara chiamata da Dio a 12 anni. Eppure si sottomise ai suoi genitori, che non capivano, e si preparò durante i successivi 18 anni. Ora il cielo si aprì, e Dio disse: “Tu sei il mio Figlio prediletto, in te mi sono compiaciuto!” Che cosa di più potremmo desiderare? Niente altro conterà se un giorno arrivassimo in cielo e ascoltassimo quelle parole.

Gesù si preparò per diciotto anni per i suoi tre anni di ministero, ma furono i tre anni di ministero più efficaci che chiunque abbia mai avuto e avrà mai. Si preparò!

Dio ha un piano per ciascuna delle nostre vite. Possiamo sottometterci alla sua guida e al suo tempo? Germiniamo, morendo a noi stessi e germogliando nella novità di vita. Stiamo in un sonno germinante. Potremmo non capire tutto, ma prepariamoci, germogliamo, cresciamo e aumentiamo nella grazia di Dio. Mio giovane fratello e mia giovane sorella, fai semplicemente un passo alla volta, e Dio benedirà la tua vita.

January 21, 1525, was the 500th anniversary of Anabaptism. Five hundred years ago, a monumental event in the history of the Christian church occurred. A small group of radical Christians quietly gathered in the home of Felix Mantz in Zürich, Switzerland. The state church government of Zürich had ordered parents to have their infants baptized or face being banished from their homes. Gathering together for Scripture studies and prayer meetings was outlawed, too. Yet, on this momentous winter evening, Feliz Mantz, Conrad Grebel, George Blaurock, and a few others took their obedience one step further. After praying and committing to serve God faithfully, George Blaurock asked Conrad Grebel to baptize him in true Christian faith, which Conrad did. The others also requested baptism, and George, in turn, also baptized them. And thus, Anabaptism, as we know it, was born.

Though these three men played a key part in Anabaptist history, the Reformation did not begin with them. The real catalyst for flaming the fires of revival was kindled 88 years earlier. In 1436, a German goldsmith named Johannes Gutenberg invented a moveable type printing press. This dramatically improved printing, and books could be printed in greater quantities. Instead of a few books only in the hands of the wealthy, the common person could now afford to buy books. The first books to be printed on the Gutenberg press were Bibles. When common folks began to buy and read Bibles, they began to realize that the darkness of religious oppression was keeping them from understanding the true light of God’s Word. And thus, the Reformation was born.

Fast forward 588 years. The printed paper still inspires men and women. But today, it is much easier to print a periodical magazine such as The Heartbeat of the Remnant. We simply take up the pen or keyboard and write. Our document is then digitally edited and electronically sent to the printer. After the files are uploaded, the printing press will print 6,000 copies in a little over 12 hours. It is then finished and mailed to 51 countries around the world and many states in the U.S. Printing has come a long way since 1436 when each page had to be set up and printed individually.

According to a 2010 Google project, just under 130 million books were published globally. Since then, UNESCO estimates that approximately 2.2 million new titles are published each year. By adding these yearly publications to the initial count, we can estimate that as of 2024, there are more than 160 million unique books in the world. This number does not account for books that may have gone out of print or been discontinued since their initial publication. The wise preacher was right when he wrote, “And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh” (Ecclesiastes 12:12).

Let’s use this freedom of the press to God’s glory while we have the chance. I work for Christian Aid Ministries, and we regularly hear testimonies from Christians in closed and restricted countries who are extremely blessed to receive Christian literature. One person from an undisclosed location wrote, “. . . we all take turns reading the magazine in church. A very edifying magazine. God bless you! God’s blessings.” Hearing testimonies like this makes me more thankful for what we have. But I’m sure people in persecuted countries value their Christian literature more highly than we who have Bibles and Christian literature in abundance.

In this issue, we reprinted two articles by request. A Glorious Church by Barry Grant and Joy in the Crevices by Sheryl Zeiset were both first printed in 2019. May our churches demonstrate the virtues and our homes radiate the beauty that is portrayed in these timeless articles.

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

21 يناير 1525 كان الذكرى الخمس مئة للحركة المعمدية الجديدة. قبل خمسمئة عام، وقع حدث ضخم في تاريخ الكنيسة المسيحية. جمعت مجموعة صغيرة من المسيحيين المتشددين بهدوء في بيت فيليكس مانتز في زيورخ بسويسرا. كانت حكومة الكنيسة الحكومية في زيورخ قد أصدرت أمراً للأهالي بتعميد رضّعهم وإلا طُردوا من منازلهم. كما حُظرت الاجتماعات للدراسات الكتابية ولقاءات الصلاة. ومع ذلك، في تلك الليلة الشتوية المصيرية، أخذ فيليز مانتز وكونراد غريبل وجورج بلوروك وعدد قليل من الآخرين طاعتهم خطوة إلى الأمام. بعد الصلاة والالتزام بخدمة الله بأمانة، طلب جورج بلوروك من كونراد غريبل أن يعمّده في الإيمان المسيحي الحقيقي، ففعل كونراد ذلك. وطلب الآخرون أيضاً المعمودية، فعمّدهم جورج بدوره. وهكذا وُلدت الحركة المعمدية الجديدة كما نعرفها.

مع أن هؤلاء الرجال الثلاثة لعبوا دوراً رئيسياً في تاريخ المعمدانية، إلا أن الإصلاح لم يبدأ بهم. الشرارة الحقيقية لإشعال نيران الصحوة أُوقدت قبل 88 عاماً. في عام 1436، اخترع صائغ ألماني يُدعى يوهانس غوتنبرغ مطبعة بأحرف متحركة. هذا حسن الطباعة بشكل كبير، فبإمكان الكتب أن تُطبَع بكميات أكبر. وبدلاً من احتفاظ الأغنياء ببضعة كتب فقط، صار الشخص العادي الآن يستطيع شراء الكتب. أولى الكتب المطبوعة على مطبعة غوتنبرغ كانت كتباً مقدّسة. عندما بدأ الناس العاديون بشراء وقراءة الكتب المقدّسة، بدأوا يدركون أن ظلام القمع الديني كان يمنعهم من فهم نور كلمة الله الحق. وهكذا وُلد الإصلاح.

تقدم سريعاً 588 عاماً. لا يزال الورق المطبوَع يُلهِم الرجال والنساء. لكن اليوم، أصبح من الأسهل بكثير طباعة مجلة دورية مثل نبض الباقين. نحن ببساطة نأخذ القلم أو لوحة المفاتيح ونكتب. يُحرَّر مستندنا رقمياً ثم يُرسل إلكترونياً إلى المطبعة. بعد رفع الملفات، ستطبع الماكينة 6000 نسخة في أقل من 12 ساعة. ثم تُنجز وتُرسل بالبريد إلى 51 دولة حول العالم وإلى ولايات عديدة في الولايات المتحدة. لقد قطعت الطباعة شوطاً طويلاً منذ 1436 عندما كان يجب إعداد كل صفحة وطبعها على حدة.

وفق مشروع جوجل لعام 2010، نُشِر ما يقارب 130 مليون كتاب على مستوى العالم. منذ ذلك الحين، تُقدِّر اليونسكو أنه يُنشر حوالي 2.2 مليون عنوان جديد سنوياً. بإضافة هذه الإصدارات السنوية إلى العدّ الأوّلي، يمكننا تقدير أنه حتى عام 2024، ثمة أكثر من 160 مليون كتاب فريد في العالم. هذا العدد لا يأخذ في الحسبان الكتب التي قد تكون خرجت من الطباعة أو توقّفت عن النشر منذ نشرها الأولي. كان الواعظ الحكيم على حق عندما كتب: «وأيضًا يا بني، تنبَّه من هذا: إن صنع كثير من الكتب لا نهاية له، وكثرة الدراسة تُتْعِب الجسدَ» (جامعة 12:12).

لنستخدم هذه الحرية في الصحافة لمجد الله ما دام أمامنا الفرصة. أعمل لدى Christian Aid Ministries، ونسمع بانتظام شهادات من مسيحيين في دول مغلقة ومقيدة الذين يُبارَكون للغاية لتلقّيهم الأدب المسيحي. كتب شخص من مكان لم يُفصح عنه: “... نحن نأخذ مناوبة قراءة المجلة في الكنيسة. مجلة مفيدة جدًا. ليبارككم الله! بركات الله.” سماع مثل هذه الشهادات يجعلني أكثر امتنانًا لما لدينا. لكنني متأكد أن الناس في البلدان المضطهدة يقدّرون أدبهم المسيحي أكثر منا الذين نمتلك أعدادًا وفيرة من الكتب المقدّسة والأدب المسيحي.

في هذا العدد، أعِدْنا نشر مقالين بناءً على طلب. نُشِر كل من "كنيسة مجيدة" لبارري غرانت و"فرح في الشقوق" لشيريل زيزت أولاً عام 2019. ليُظهر قُرانا فضائلَهم ولتُضيء بيوتنا بالجمال المبثوث في هذين المقالين الخالدين.

بركات للجميع،

إدوارد مارتن
